questions.question: Which description best defines a blockchain?

options.text: A centralized ledger in which one operator alone finalizes every record
A method for managing secret keys used to decrypt data
A distributed ledger in which multiple participants share records according to rules
A compression method that reduces files and restores their original contents

questions.explanation: Blockchain is a technology in which multiple participants share ledger records and update them through defined procedures. Specific participation permissions and consensus mechanisms vary by implementation.
questions.learningObjective: The basic concept of a distributed ledger

questions.question: What unit in a blockchain groups transaction records and other data together with related metadata?
questions.explanation: A block consists of data, such as transactions, and a header describing that block. The exact format can vary between blockchains.
questions.learningObjective: The role of a block

questions.question: What key information links a Bitcoin block to the immediately preceding block?

options.text: The number of transactions in the previous block
The total fees in the previous block
The public address of the previous block's recipient
The hash of the previous block's header

questions.explanation: A Bitcoin block header contains the hash of the previous block's header. This reference links the blocks together.
questions.learningObjective: Information used to reference the previous block

questions.question: What is the first block in a blockchain called?
questions.explanation: The genesis block is the first block and the starting point of a blockchain.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of a genesis block

questions.question: What is an individual system that participates in a blockchain network and runs the required software called?
questions.explanation: A node is an individual system that forms part of a blockchain network. Its roles, such as storage, validation, and propagation, depend on the node type.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of a node

questions.question: Which statement best describes a P2P network?

options.text: One node's local records take precedence over all other records without validation
Every data exchange requires a single central server
Nodes cannot transmit data directly to one another
Participating nodes exchange data with one another

questions.explanation: In a P2P structure, participants connect to one another and exchange data. Blocks and transactions can also propagate through connected nodes.
questions.learningObjective: The structure of P2P communication

questions.question: What is the main reason a blockchain needs a consensus process?

options.text: To automatically make all transaction contents private
To allow participating nodes to agree on valid ledger records
To automatically recover signing keys lost by users
To fix the exchange price of every token at one value

questions.explanation: Consensus determines which records and ordering distributed participants will accept. It is not a process for standardizing market prices or user passwords.
questions.learningObjective: The purpose of consensus

questions.question: What is a key task a Bitcoin full node performs when it receives a new block?

options.text: It checks whether the block complies with the consensus rules it enforces
It accepts the block simply because it is the largest
It skips checking transaction contents as long as proof of work is present
It accepts the block only if it contains a transaction the node created

questions.explanation: A full node independently checks whether a received block satisfies the consensus rules. A block is not valid merely because a miner sent it.
questions.learningObjective: Independent validation by full nodes

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes participation in block production on a permissionless blockchain?

options.text: Participants join under the protocol's conditions without prior permission from a designated administrator
Every participant receives a certificate from the same company
Only representatives of contracted companies participate in a fixed rotation
Only employee accounts approved by a central company can participate

questions.explanation: A permissionless structure allows participation without prior approval from a designated administrator. Producing blocks still requires meeting the protocol's conditions, such as proof of work.
questions.learningObjective: Participation in permissionless networks

questions.question: Which statement best describes a permissioned blockchain?

options.text: All participants operating the network share the same private key
An approval process restricts who can perform certain roles, such as producing blocks
Transactions from approved participants do not need to follow consensus rules
Everyone must be granted all permissions, including both reading and writing

questions.explanation: A permissioned network authorizes participants to perform specific roles. Read access and permission to submit transactions can be designed separately.
questions.learningObjective: Participation restrictions in permissioned networks

questions.question: Several approved logistics companies jointly set participation rules and operate a ledger. Which term best describes this arrangement?

options.text: Permissionless operation open to the public
Exclusive operation by a single organization

questions.explanation: In a consortium, multiple organizations jointly participate in operations and governance. They can also jointly define rules for adding or removing participants.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of consortium operation

questions.question: Which is the broadest description of a transaction in a blockchain?

options.text: A unit of recovery information used to regenerate keys
A list of all nodes participating in consensus
A record requesting an asset transfer, a data change, or another action
A block that groups and links multiple transactions

questions.explanation: Transactions are used not only to transfer assets but also to execute smart contracts or change business data.
questions.learningObjective: The scope of transactions

questions.question: What does a cryptographic hash function compute from input data?

options.text: A digital signature created using a secret key
A compressed file from which the original can be restored

questions.explanation: A hash function transforms input into a digest with a defined format. Hash values are used for purposes such as identifying data and checking its integrity.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of a hash value

questions.question: What happens when the same hash function is independently applied twice to the same byte data?

options.text: The result changes depending on the time of computation
The result changes depending on the type of device
Both computations produce the same hash value
Each computation produces a different random value

questions.explanation: A hash function is deterministic. The same input and algorithm produce the same result regardless of the time or device used for computation.
questions.learningObjective: Determinism in hash computation

questions.question: What is the main purpose of comparing a reliably stored hash of an original document with the hash of a document received later?

options.text: To check whether the document's byte contents have changed
To recover the original document from the hash value
To encrypt and hide all the document's contents
To authenticate the author's identity using only the hash

questions.explanation: Comparing values produced by the same hash algorithm helps check integrity against the original. A hash alone does not verify the author's identity or the truth of the contents.
questions.learningObjective: Checking for file changes after recording

questions.question: Which statement describes the one-way property of a secure cryptographic hash function?

options.text: Finding an input that produces a given hash value is computationally difficult
The hash stores a compressed version of the original even when the input is not saved
A publicly available decryption key restores the original exactly
It randomly changes the result each time even for identical input

questions.explanation: A secure hash function is designed to make it difficult to find a corresponding input from its output. However, short, predictable inputs may be guessed by trying possible candidates.
questions.learningObjective: The one-way property of hashing

questions.question: What is the main purpose of attaching a digital signature to a blockchain transaction?

options.text: To automatically hide the transaction contents on the public ledger
To immediately guarantee block inclusion and final confirmation
To automatically certify delivery of physical goods associated with the transaction
To allow verification that the transaction was signed with the corresponding private key

questions.explanation: A digital signature verifies authorization associated with a private key and the integrity of the signed data. A signature does not itself encrypt the transaction contents.
questions.learningObjective: The basic purpose of a digital signature

questions.question: In a typical public-key-based wallet, which key must be kept secret when creating transaction signatures?
questions.explanation: The private key is used to create transaction signatures. It must be kept secret because someone who obtains it may be able to move the assets.
questions.learningObjective: The key used for signing

questions.question: What does another person use to verify a typical digital signature?

options.text: The recipient's own wallet recovery phrase
The public key corresponding to the signer
Only the hash of the signed data

questions.explanation: A digital signature can be verified using the public key. There is no need to give the verifier the signer's private key or recovery phrase.
questions.learningObjective: The key used to verify signatures

questions.question: Someone wants to send coins to your wallet. What information would you generally provide?

options.text: Your receiving address on the relevant network

questions.explanation: The sender uses the receiving address to specify the recipient. Receiving assets does not require disclosing a private key or recovery phrase.
questions.learningObjective: Information to provide when receiving assets

questions.question: What task does a receiving QR code on a Bitcoin payment screen mainly make easier?

options.text: Verifying the proof of work of a received block
Guaranteeing final confirmation of a submitted transaction
Replacing a secure backup of the wallet's private key
Entering a receiving address and payment information

questions.explanation: A receiving QR code helps enter an address or payment-request details. After scanning, check that the displayed receiving information is what you intended.
questions.learningObjective: The purpose of payment QR codes

questions.question: Which statement about Bitcoin addresses and personal information is correct?

options.text: Every address must store the user's real name and contact details
Records are address-based, but linking them to external information can reveal an identity
Changing an address also deletes past public transaction records
Anyone who knows a public address can immediately calculate its private key

questions.explanation: Bitcoin does not guarantee complete anonymity. Combining public transaction histories with information about service usage and other sources may identify an individual.
questions.learningObjective: Bitcoin's pseudonymity

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a securely generated public and private key pair?

options.text: The public key can be derived from the private key, while the reverse calculation is practically difficult
The public and private keys are always the same value displayed differently
Knowing the public key lets anyone obtain the private key through ordinary decryption
The private key is published to verify signatures, while the public key is kept secret

questions.explanation: Public-key cryptography relies on the difference in computational difficulty between deriving a public key from a private key and performing the reverse calculation.
questions.learningObjective: The asymmetric relationship between public and private keys

questions.question: Which description best explains the role of a blockchain wallet app?

options.text: A system that automatically converts wallet addresses into real bank accounts
A consensus administrator that alone allocates block-production rights
A server that manages the network's only copy of the ledger
A tool that manages keys and helps users view accounts and sign transactions

questions.explanation: A wallet is a tool for interacting with accounts. Asset state is recorded on the ledger, while the wallet helps users view that state, authorize transactions, and perform related actions.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing wallets from ledgers

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the recovery phrase provided when a seed-based wallet is first created?

options.text: To restore the wallet's keys and accounts
To serve as a public receiving address to give to others
To serve as a shared password for logging in to ordinary websites
To serve as a transaction number for tracking an individual transfer

questions.explanation: The recovery phrase is essential information for restoring the wallet's keys. The information required for recovery can vary depending on the supported method and whether an additional passphrase is used.
questions.learningObjective: The purpose of a recovery phrase

questions.question: Who generally directly controls signing authority over assets in a self-custody wallet?

options.text: The operator of an explorer displaying the address
The miner who produced the latest block
The user who holds the wallet's private key
The company that developed the wallet app

questions.explanation: In a self-custody wallet, the user manages the keys. Backing up keys and preventing their exposure are therefore important user responsibilities.
questions.learningObjective: Responsibilities in self-custody wallets

questions.question: In a custodial service where an exchange holds the private keys for customer assets, what do users particularly depend on?

options.text: Wallet backup copies held by other customers
Customer-specific withdrawal approval from miners on the underlying chain
The operator's custody security and asset management
The block explorer operator's management of exchange passwords

questions.explanation: Because the operator holds the keys in a custodial service, users must trust its security and honest asset management. The service also affects account access and withdrawals.
questions.learningObjective: Who must be trusted in a custodial service

questions.question: Which criterion best identifies a hot wallet?

options.text: The environment in which its keys are used is connected to the internet
It is a watch-only account that cannot create transactions
It signs only on devices completely isolated from networks
Its keys are always printed only on a single sheet of paper

questions.explanation: A hot wallet uses its keys in an online environment. It offers convenient access but requires protection against online attacks.
questions.learningObjective: The characteristics of a hot wallet

questions.question: What is the main purpose of cold storage?

options.text: To isolate private keys from environments exposed to online attacks
To complete transfers without network validation
To eliminate the need to store a recovery phrase
To hide every transaction record from the public ledger

questions.explanation: Cold storage reduces online risk by isolating keys from networks. Protection against lost backups and physical access is also necessary.
questions.learningObjective: The purpose of cold storage

questions.question: What is a typical security feature of a hardware wallet?

options.text: It restores a lost private key using only a receiving address
It provides only keyless viewing of public transactions
It protects private keys and signs inside a dedicated device
It entrusts private keys exclusively to a cloud server and signs remotely

questions.explanation: A hardware wallet is designed to sign inside a dedicated device that protects its keys. Users must also check the transaction details displayed on the device.
questions.learningObjective: The main function of a hardware wallet

questions.question: What does the unlock password of a typical self-custody wallet app mainly protect?

options.text: Searching for the address on the public ledger
Using an already copied recovery phrase on another device
Validating transactions from that address across the network
Access to wallet data stored in that app or device

questions.explanation: A wallet lock protects local access or stored keys. It does not put a password on the entire public ledger.
questions.learningObjective: The protection scope of a wallet unlock password

questions.question: What can a watch-only wallet do when it contains only public information, such as addresses, and no private keys?

options.text: Freely withdraw assets from the address
Erase transactions associated with the address from the ledger
Check the balance and transaction history of registered addresses
Automatically reissue the private key for the address

questions.explanation: A watch-only wallet checks state using public information. Without the keys required to sign, it cannot spend assets under that authority.
questions.learningObjective: The capabilities of a watch-only wallet

questions.question: A wallet requires signatures from 2 of 3 distinct keys. What is the minimum number of signatures needed to authorize a transaction?
questions.explanation: A 2-of-3 multisignature condition requires valid signatures from two distinct keys among the three registered keys.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding multisignature requirements

questions.question: Which approach protects wallet backups while reducing the risk of a fire or loss at one location?

options.text: Keeping the wallet device and the only backup together in one bag
Storing the recovery phrase only as plaintext in your email
Keeping only a photo of the receiving address instead of a private-key backup
Keeping backups in separate secure locations with controlled access

questions.explanation: Backups in multiple protected locations reduce the risk of losing every recovery method in one incident. Access to each backup must be controlled as the number of backups increases.
questions.learningObjective: Reducing a single point of failure in backups

questions.question: Which transaction process correctly uses offline signing?

options.text: Submitting an unsigned transaction created offline to the network without signing it
Recording a transaction in a block immediately after offline signing without network propagation
Keeping only addresses on the offline device and copying private keys to the online device
Signing on an offline device and broadcasting the signed transaction through an online device

questions.explanation: Transaction creation, signing, and broadcasting can be separated. A setup can use keys on an offline device and pass only the signed transaction online.
questions.learningObjective: Separating offline signing from online broadcasting

questions.question: What does it mean to broadcast a signed transaction to the network?

options.text: To confirm that the transaction has been included in a block
To complete the proof of work for a new block
To create a private-key backup on a local device
To send the transaction information to nodes

questions.explanation: Broadcasting propagates a transaction. Propagation alone does not guarantee block inclusion or confirmation.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of broadcasting a transaction

questions.question: What is the waiting area in which a node keeps candidate transactions that have not yet been included in a block commonly called?
questions.explanation: The mempool holds transactions that a node has awaiting processing. Not every node's mempool is always identical.
questions.learningObjective: The role of the mempool

questions.question: What does it mean when a Bitcoin on-chain transaction receives its first confirmation?

options.text: The wallet has only finished signing the transaction
The transaction has been included in an accepted block
The recipient has opened the wallet's deposit screen
The transaction has reached one node's waiting list

questions.explanation: An on-chain transaction receives its first confirmation when it is included in a block. The confirmation count increases as subsequent blocks are added.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of a Bitcoin transaction's first confirmation

questions.question: You want to find one specific transaction you sent in a block explorer. What is the most direct information to search with?

options.text: The saved nickname of the receiving address
The total balance of the sending address
The latest block number on the network

questions.explanation: A transaction hash or TXID identifies an individual transaction. A wallet's local nickname or password is not information for searching public transactions.
questions.learningObjective: Using transaction identifiers

questions.question: What is a typical use of a block explorer?

options.text: Holding users' private keys to provide asset custody
Arbitrarily modifying the recipient address of an existing transaction
Viewing public data about blocks, transactions, and addresses
Setting the network's consensus rules on behalf of users

questions.explanation: A block explorer is an interface for viewing blockchain data. A lookup service does not grant control over the ledger or keys.
questions.learningObjective: The basic purpose of a block explorer

questions.question: What does the block height or block number displayed in a block explorer mainly indicate?

options.text: The total transaction fees paid in the block
The number of transactions included in the block
The block's position in the chain
The total size of the block's data in bytes

questions.explanation: Block height is a number indicating a block's position relative to the start of the chain. It does not mean the transaction count or an asset price.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of block height

questions.question: What does a block's timestamp represent?

options.text: The exact time every sender pressed the send button
The time the recipient first viewed the deposit
The block's time information recorded according to protocol rules
The time every node received the block simultaneously

questions.explanation: A timestamp represents a block's time information. It follows implementation-specific rules and does not prove the exact real-world time of every transaction.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of a block timestamp

questions.question: What can you generally check by entering a public address in an Ethereum block explorer?

options.text: Passwords for every device managing the address
The address's on-chain balance and transaction history

questions.explanation: An explorer displays public information such as an address's balance and transaction records. Private keys and recovery phrases are not information published on the ledger.
questions.learningObjective: Information that can be looked up by address

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a role of blockchain transaction fees?

options.text: They guarantee an exchange a fixed percentage of the amount of every ordinary transfer
They charge for network resource use and provide incentives for processing
They grant permission to skip signature verification
They purchase a protocol recovery service when keys are lost

questions.explanation: Fees charge for resources used by transactions and incentivize processing. How fees are distributed or burned varies by protocol.
questions.learningObjective: The function of network fees

questions.question: When setting a Bitcoin on-chain transaction fee, what factor is particularly important besides the amount being transferred?

options.text: A fixed percentage applied uniformly to the amount of BTC sent
The transaction's data size and demand for block space
The physical distance between sender and recipient
Only how long the BTC has been held in the wallet

questions.explanation: Bitcoin fees are not simply proportional to the amount of BTC being sent. The space occupied by a transaction and demand for processing are important.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing Bitcoin fees from transfer amounts

questions.question: What is the main purpose of sending a small test transfer before sending a large amount to a new recipient?

options.text: To obtain protocol-level cancellation rights for later transactions
To automatically correct a changed address in a later transfer
To check that the address and receiving route work as intended
To fix the block-inclusion time of a later transaction in advance

questions.explanation: A small test transfer helps verify the receiving information. The address and conditions must still be checked again for subsequent transfers.
questions.learningObjective: The purpose of a small test transfer

questions.question: What should you check first on a wallet's transfer-confirmation screen before signing?

options.text: Whether the coin's total circulating supply is unchanged from the previous day
Whether the latest block has the same transaction count as the preceding block
Whether the actual recipient address, amount, and fee match your intention
Whether the total network node count is unchanged from your previous lookup

questions.explanation: Signing authorizes the displayed transaction, so you must check the recipient, amount, and other details. A familiar appearance alone does not make a transaction safe.
questions.learningObjective: Checking receiving information before signing

questions.question: What does gas measure on Ethereum?

options.text: The ETH price paid for one unit of a resource
The resources required for operations such as computation
The number of token types held by an address
The quantity of ETH being transferred itself

questions.explanation: Gas measures the resources needed for computation and execution on Ethereum. Fees are calculated using gas consumed and the price per unit of gas.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of gas

questions.question: At the protocol level, what native asset pays gas fees on Ethereum mainnet?
questions.explanation: Gas fees on Ethereum mainnet are paid in ETH. Even if an app offers another payment method or pays on a user's behalf, this must be distinguished from the fee asset of the underlying network.
questions.learningObjective: Ethereum's native fee asset

questions.question: What does the gas limit of an Ethereum transaction mean?

options.text: The maximum number of tokens the recipient can receive
The price paid to buy one unit of gas
The maximum ETH balance a wallet can hold
The maximum amount of gas the transaction is allowed to use

questions.explanation: The gas limit is the upper bound on the gas a transaction may consume. The gas limit and the price per unit of gas are different values.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of the gas limit

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes fees for a transaction that was included in an Ethereum block and executed but failed?

options.text: The recipient must pay the gas cost of the failed transaction
The gas consumed during execution may still incur a cost
All gas costs are always refunded if the transaction fails
A failed transaction uses no network resources

questions.explanation: A transaction executed in a block incurs the cost of the gas it uses even if it fails and its state changes are reverted. This must be distinguished from a transaction rejected at submission.
questions.learningObjective: The relationship between execution failure and fees

questions.question: What does the nonce represent in a transaction sent by a typical Ethereum externally owned account?

options.text: A counter that distinguishes the sequence of transactions sent by that account
The confirmed height of the block that will include the transaction
The unit price of gas required for execution
An input repeatedly varied to change a block's proof-of-work hash

questions.explanation: The nonce in an ordinary EOA transaction is an account-specific sequence counter. It distinguishes transactions from the same account and helps prevent replay.
questions.learningObjective: The role of the nonce in ordinary EOA transactions

questions.question: Which description best defines a double-spending attempt?

options.text: An attempt to reuse the same spendable asset in different transactions
Paying a network fee separately from the transaction amount
Creating separate recovery phrases for two different wallets
Splitting a payment between two different recipients in one transaction

questions.explanation: Double spending is an attempt to spend the same asset twice. It differs from a legitimate split payment or paying a fee.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of double spending

questions.question: What is the main task a block producer performs in Bitcoin's proof of work?

options.text: Announcing a block solely according to a predetermined operator rotation
Finding a block-header hash that meets the difficulty target
Depositing assets to participate in validation and attestations
Checking only the identity certificates of authorized operators

questions.explanation: Bitcoin proof of work involves repeated computation to find a block-header hash that satisfies a specified target condition.
questions.learningObjective: The core mechanism of proof of work

questions.question: What is a typical role of a Bitcoin miner?

options.text: Arbitrarily reversing all confirmed transactions at customers' request
Building a candidate block containing transactions and performing proof of work
Issuing as many reward coins as desired regardless of consensus rules
Issuing private keys on behalf of other users to authorize their transactions

questions.explanation: Miners select transactions, build candidate blocks, and try to satisfy the proof-of-work requirement. Other nodes must validate the resulting blocks.
questions.learningObjective: The role of miners

questions.question: What does a node do to validate a proof-of-work result it receives?

options.text: It checks whether the submitted block-header hash satisfies the target condition
It repeats every failed computation the miner attempted from the beginning
It accepts the result based only on the miner's deposit
It compares only the BTC balance of the miner who submitted the proof

questions.explanation: Finding a valid hash may take many attempts, while checking whether a submitted result meets the condition is relatively simple.
questions.learningObjective: The difference between searching for and verifying proof of work

questions.question: Which consensus mechanism uses validators' deposited assets as the basis for economic accountability?
questions.explanation: Proof of stake uses assets deposited by validators as the basis for network participation and economic penalties.
questions.learningObjective: Identifying proof of stake

questions.question: Which task is appropriate for an Ethereum proof-of-stake validator?

options.text: Validating new blocks and participating in proposals and attestations according to its assigned role
Collecting every sender's private key to sign on their behalf
Accepting received blocks in arrival order without checking rules
Repeatedly computing a proof-of-work target hash as a requirement for proposing blocks

questions.explanation: Validators check blocks and state changes and participate in consensus. Becoming a validator does not grant access to other accounts' keys or permission to modify contracts.
questions.learningObjective: The work of a validator

questions.question: Why does a protocol mainly provide block rewards?

options.text: To allow nodes to ignore consensus rules
To incentivize legitimate participation needed to maintain the network
To guarantee recipients the principal amount of a transaction
To make the market prices of all coins equal

questions.explanation: Block rewards are an economic mechanism that incentivizes the work and participation required by the protocol. Reward structures vary between networks.
questions.learningObjective: The purpose of protocol rewards

questions.question: What does slashing mean in Ethereum proof of stake?

options.text: A penalty that reduces a validator's deposited assets for specific consensus violations
The procedure for normally ending validation and receiving deposited assets back
A transaction that splits received assets among other addresses
The network fee an ordinary sender pays for transaction processing

questions.explanation: Slashing penalizes specific rule violations, such as signing conflicting messages. It does not refer to every ordinary error or temporary disconnection.
questions.learningObjective: The basic meaning of slashing

questions.question: When discussing changes to blockchain protocol rules, what is the term fork most closely associated with?

options.text: Changes to software rules and compatibility between versions
Encoding receiving addresses and checking for typos
Backing up recovery phrases and moving between devices
Propagating unconfirmed transactions and node waiting lists

questions.explanation: A protocol fork concerns changes to blockchain rules. Soft forks and hard forks are distinguished by their compatibility with existing rules.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of a protocol fork

questions.question: Which unit is used to express small amounts of bitcoin?
questions.explanation: A satoshi is a unit of bitcoin. Wei and gwei are units of ETH, while gas measures resource usage on Ethereum.
questions.learningObjective: The name of Bitcoin's small unit

questions.question: What does UTXO mean in Bitcoin?

options.text: A transaction output that has already been spent
A draft transaction that has not been signed
A transaction output that has not yet been spent
A list of transactions waiting for block inclusion

questions.explanation: UTXO stands for Unspent Transaction Output. It is an unspent output that can be used in a later transaction by satisfying its spending conditions.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of UTXO

questions.question: When Bitcoin inputs exceed the sum of the payment amount and fee, how is the remaining amount usually handled?

options.text: The remainder must be sent as an additional payment to the recipient
Only part of the original input is spent and the same input is left in place
A change output is created to an address controlled by the sender
It is omitted on the assumption that the recipient will return it voluntarily later

questions.explanation: Bitcoin spends outputs in full and creates new outputs. To receive the remaining amount back, a change output is usually created.
questions.learningObjective: The purpose of a change output

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between Ethereum and ether (ETH)?

options.text: Ethereum and ETH are two independent blockchains
Ethereum is the network, and ETH is its native cryptoasset
Ethereum is an account address, and ETH is that address's private key
Ethereum is a token, and ETH is the wallet that stores it

questions.explanation: Ethereum refers to the blockchain network and platform, while ether is that network's native cryptoasset.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing Ethereum from ether

questions.question: What directly controls the authority to sign transactions for a typical Ethereum externally owned account (EOA)?

options.text: The private key corresponding to the account
The public hash of the latest transaction
The numeric value of the account's next nonce

questions.explanation: Transaction authorization for a typical EOA is controlled through signatures made with the corresponding private key. Account types should not be determined solely by whether they contain code.
questions.learningObjective: Control of a typical externally owned account

questions.question: What directly determines the behavior of an Ethereum smart contract account?

options.text: The latest source file stored only on the developer's computer
The contract description displayed in a block explorer
An arbitrary explanation supplied by the person calling it
The rules of the code deployed to that account

questions.explanation: A smart contract account behaves according to its deployed program logic. Whether it includes administrative powers also depends on the contract's design.
questions.learningObjective: Execution rules of a contract account

questions.question: Which description best defines a smart contract?

options.text: A program and state deployed to execute on a blockchain
The digital-signature string attached to a transaction itself
A compressed ledger file transmitted between nodes
Any image of a paper contract stored as a file on a blockchain

questions.explanation: A smart contract is a program that operates with code and state at a specific address. This is different from simply uploading a document.
questions.learningObjective: The definition of a smart contract

questions.question: What does deploying a smart contract to Ethereum mean?

options.text: Only uploading its source code to a public repository
Only compiling its source code on the developer's computer
Registering contract code through a transaction so it can be used on the network
Saving a nickname for the contract address in a wallet

questions.explanation: Deploying a contract creates an executable contract on the network and is handled as a transaction on Ethereum. Saving a file locally does not deploy it.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of contract deployment

questions.question: Which language is widely used to write Ethereum smart contracts?
questions.explanation: Solidity is a language used to write Ethereum smart contracts. The code is compiled into a deployable form.
questions.learningObjective: Identifying a smart contract language

questions.question: Which description best defines a decentralized application (dapp)?

options.text: Any app that encrypts a database on a central server
An application that can run only on Bitcoin mining equipment
Only an app that must store everything, including its interface and images, on-chain
An application that uses decentralized-network functions such as smart contracts

questions.explanation: A dapp uses functionality that runs on a decentralized network. Some components, such as the user interface, may depend on separate servers or services.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of a dapp

questions.question: A user wants to execute a function that changes an Ethereum smart contract's state. What action is generally required?

options.text: Sending only a read request that does not change state
Only saving the source code on their computer
Signing and submitting a transaction that calls the function
Adding the contract address to the wallet's contacts

questions.explanation: A contract state change can be requested through a transaction that calls a function. This differs from viewing a webpage or looking up an address.
questions.learningObjective: Requesting execution of a contract function

questions.question: Which is an example of a smart contract's state?

options.text: Visitor access logs on a block explorer's web server
Debugging settings stored locally in a development tool
The points balance for each address stored by the contract
An account nickname saved locally in a user's wallet app

questions.explanation: State is data that a contract stores and reads or changes during execution. It differs from interface settings outside the contract.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of contract state

questions.question: What component supplies a smart contract with temperature information from outside the blockchain?
questions.explanation: An oracle retrieves external data and supplies it in a form that a smart contract can use.
questions.learningObjective: The basic role of an oracle

questions.question: An external access-control device should open a door when an on-chain payment is confirmed. What role does an outbound oracle integration play?

options.text: It displays existing public transaction information only on a webpage
It synchronizes a ledger copy to a new validating node
It delivers the on-chain result in a form the external system can use
It brings external temperature information into an on-chain contract

questions.explanation: Oracles can deliver on-chain results to external systems as well as bring external information on-chain. Separate integration is needed to operate the physical device.
questions.learningObjective: Delivering on-chain results to external systems

questions.question: Which example illustrates composability between Ethereum smart contracts?

options.text: Changing a developer's local code changes every existing contract
Contracts on the same network cannot call one another's functions
Giving two contracts the same name automatically combines their balances
One contract calls another contract's public function to use its functionality

questions.explanation: Contracts can use callable functions offered by other contracts to build larger services. Access conditions and call results follow each contract's rules.
questions.learningObjective: Composability between contracts

questions.question: What does deterministic execution of a smart contract mean?

options.text: Functions with the same name always produce the same result even when the current state differs
Nodes can arbitrarily choose the result of the same transaction
The contract's calculation results vary with the manufacturer of a node's computer
The same state and execution inputs produce the same result

questions.explanation: For nodes to validate the same transaction, execution results must agree under the same conditions. Contract execution inputs also include the execution environment provided by the protocol.
questions.learningObjective: Why deterministic execution is needed

questions.question: What does minting generally mean for an NFT?

options.text: Issuing a new token and creating its identity and ownership records
Transferring an existing token to another address
Only looking up the trading history of an already issued token
Burning an existing token to remove it from circulation

questions.explanation: Minting creates a new token according to contract rules. For NFTs, a unique identifier and ownership records are managed along with it.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of minting

questions.question: What property means that one token is treated as equivalent to another token of the same type?
questions.explanation: Fungible tokens can be treated as equivalent when their type and quantity are the same. This distinguishes them from NFTs, where each token's uniqueness matters.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of fungibility

questions.question: What key feature distinguishes an NFT from an ordinary fungible token?

options.text: It is designed to maintain a fixed price relative to a particular currency
It uniquely identifies each individual token
Units of the same type are equivalent without individual distinctions
It is used only as the network's native gas-fee unit

questions.explanation: An NFT represents the uniqueness of an individual token. Uniqueness does not guarantee value or a selling price.
questions.learningObjective: The characteristics of NFTs

questions.question: What value distinguishes a particular NFT within one NFT contract?

options.text: The displayed size of the image file
The token's most recent sale price

questions.explanation: An NFT contract assigns identifiers to individual tokens. The network and contract must also be specified to avoid confusion with the same number in another contract.
questions.learningObjective: Checking NFT identifiers

questions.question: What is additional NFT information, such as its name, description, and image reference, commonly called?
questions.explanation: Metadata describes what an NFT represents and its attributes. Its storage location and whether it can be changed depend on the implementation.
questions.learningObjective: The purpose of NFT metadata

questions.question: Why might numbered-seat concert tickets be represented as NFTs?

options.text: To publish the ticket holder's private key
To make every seat's location and price identical
To detect attendance without any external input
To manage each ticket's unique identity and ownership records

questions.explanation: NFTs can identify tickets with different individual attributes, such as seats. Actual admission verification requires a separately designed service.
questions.learningObjective: Using NFTs for tickets

questions.question: You save an image linked to someone else's NFT on your computer. What changes from that action alone?

options.text: The NFT's on-chain owner address changes to your address
The existing NFT receives a new token ID
The transfer record in the NFT contract is modified to your address
A copy of the image is created on your computer

questions.explanation: Copying a file and transferring an NFT's ownership record are separate actions. Changing on-chain ownership requires the transfer procedure specified by the contract.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing file copying from NFT transfers

questions.question: What do stablecoins generally aim to achieve?

options.text: Fixing every transaction fee on the network
Maintaining a stable value relative to a reference asset or currency
Keeping the transaction count in every block constant
Making their exchange prices against all other tokens identical

questions.explanation: Stablecoins are designed to target value stability relative to a particular reference. Stabilization methods, including collateral and issuance mechanisms, vary.
questions.learningObjective: The design objective of a stablecoin

questions.question: What is the main role of reserves or collateral in a collateral-backed stablecoin?

options.text: They provide a recovery deposit for reissuing users' private keys
They permanently pay gas fees on behalf of every user
They support the token's value-maintenance and redemption structure
They are used only as deposits to penalize validators for consensus violations

questions.explanation: Reserves are assets that back the value of collateral-backed tokens. Their adequacy, custody, redemption conditions, and other details must be checked for each design.
questions.learningObjective: The role of reserve assets

questions.question: What should you particularly examine when a company issues a stablecoin backed by fiat-currency reserves it holds?

options.text: Only the total assets staked by validators on the underlying chain
Only the total computing power of mining equipment on the underlying chain
Only the gas limit selected by the recipient in their wallet
The issuer's reserves and operational redemption structure

questions.explanation: A fiat-backed structure depends on the issuer holding the reserves. It is important to check whether sufficient reserves exist.
questions.learningObjective: Issuer dependence in fiat-backed stablecoins

questions.question: Which description best defines DeFi?

options.text: Financial services that use blockchains and smart contracts
The wallet function of generating and backing up private keys itself
Ordinary internet banking managed only within a bank's internal systems
The node communication protocol that propagates blocks itself

questions.explanation: DeFi is a category of services that provide financial functions, such as lending and exchange, through blockchains and smart contracts.
questions.learningObjective: The scope of DeFi

questions.question: What is a service that uses smart contracts to exchange one token for another called?
questions.explanation: A DEX provides trading functions such as token swaps. Contract risks and exchange conditions must be assessed separately.
questions.learningObjective: The basic function of a DEX

questions.question: What is collateral in a DeFi loan that requires it?

options.text: The public address used to look up the lending contract
The interest the user will have to repay itself
Assets pledged to support repayment of borrowed assets
The gas fee consumed by the loan-application transaction

questions.explanation: Collateral is an asset provided to support loan repayment. The required ratio and liquidation conditions follow the service's rules.
questions.learningObjective: The meaning of collateral in a secured loan

questions.question: What does a liquidity pool generally refer to in DeFi?

options.text: A waiting list of transactions not yet included in a block
A collection of block headers received by validators
A list of unspent transaction outputs grouped by address
Assets pooled in a contract for functions such as trading or lending

questions.explanation: A liquidity pool uses assets gathered in a smart contract for functions such as exchange or lending. Specific operating rules vary by service.
questions.learningObjective: The basic concept of a liquidity pool

questions.question: Which technical risk still needs to be assessed when using a financial service operated by smart contracts?

options.text: The mere fact that the contract address is public and can be looked up
Vulnerabilities in contract code or incorrect permission settings
The mere use of a publicly available standard hash algorithm
The mere existence of decimal places in token amounts

questions.explanation: Running on a blockchain does not guarantee that contract code is correct. Vulnerabilities or excessive permissions can lead to asset losses.
questions.learningObjective: Implementation risks in smart-contract-based services

questions.question: What is the main benefit of multiple companies sharing production, transport, and receiving records in a food supply chain?

options.text: Jointly tracing the stages an asset has passed through and its record history
Automatically discovering temperatures that sensors did not measure
Determining actual product quality without any input
Automatically eliminating all physical delivery delays

questions.explanation: A shared ledger helps multiple organizations check histories and origins. A process is also needed to ensure real-world information is entered accurately.
questions.learningObjective: The purpose of supply-chain traceability

questions.question: Competing companies need to share some transaction records only with selected participants. Which Hyperledger Fabric feature is relevant?

options.text: A feature that replicates the entire transaction ledger to every organization
A feature that creates new addresses for each organization without changing read permissions
Channels that create separate ledgers for participating groups
A feature that only reduces block size without changing access rights

questions.explanation: Fabric channels allow participating groups to maintain separate transaction ledgers. They help design permissions and disclosure scope around business requirements.
questions.learningObjective: Selective sharing of transaction information between companies

questions.question: A faulty sensor records an incorrect temperature on a blockchain. Which explanation is most appropriate?

options.text: If the record's hash matches, a real measurement error is also ruled out
A large number of consensus nodes automatically verifies the sensor's measurement accuracy
A digital signature on the sensor value certifies the measurement's accuracy
Preserving the record history does not guarantee the actual temperature is correct

questions.explanation: A blockchain manages submitted records but cannot independently verify external facts. Separate data-collection and verification processes are needed.
questions.learningObjective: The limits of the truthfulness of external inputs

questions.question: What is the main concern when sensitive personal information is stored as plaintext on a publicly readable blockchain?

options.text: Plaintext is automatically encrypted because the ledger is public
The information is widely exposed, and existing copies are difficult to retrieve
Only the signer can read plaintext in a public block
Deleting it from a personal wallet app simultaneously removes every copy

questions.explanation: Public-ledger data can be replicated in many places. Sensitive-information storage must be designed with disclosure scope and the difficulty of deletion in mind.
questions.learningObjective: Considerations when publicly recording sensitive information

questions.question: Someone claiming to be wallet support asks you to send your recovery phrase. What is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Provide the phrase if they are support staff and the wallet holds only a small amount
Do not provide the phrase, and independently verify the official support channel
Assume entering the phrase is safe if the received link uses HTTPS
Split the phrase into two halves and send both to the same person

questions.explanation: Impersonating support and requesting recovery phrases or private keys is a common theft tactic. Verifying support does not require handing over control of your assets.
questions.learningObjective: Identifying phishing requests

questions.question: How can you reduce unnecessary risk when approving a smart contract to spend tokens?

options.text: Check that the contract is the intended one and limit approval to the amount needed
Assume disconnecting from the site later automatically revokes the approval
Grant every contract an unlimited allowance once the wallet connection succeeds
Check only the token balance without reading the allowance limit

questions.explanation: A spending approval grants a contract authority to use tokens. Checking the approved spender and limit can reduce risks arising from excessive permissions.
questions.learningObjective: Managing token spending approval limits

questions.question: What is a main reason to update wallet and node software through official channels?

options.text: To arbitrarily increase balances on the public ledger
To apply security fixes and feature improvements
To make all confirmed transactions unconfirmed again
To receive a lost private key from the network

questions.explanation: Software updates are important for applying fixes to known vulnerabilities or errors. The authenticity of the distribution channel must also be checked.
questions.learningObjective: The purpose of official software updates

questions.question: Which requirement most strongly supports a need to adopt blockchain?

options.text: A single server's decisions must be used unchanged without shared validation
Multiple independent parties need to share and validate a common ledger
Each party's records are independent and do not need to be shared
Only one operator's temporary data needs to be edited and deleted quickly

questions.explanation: Before choosing a technology, examine actual needs, such as shared records and trust issues among multiple parties. A centralized database may be more appropriate in some cases.
questions.learningObjective: Assessing whether blockchain adoption is suitable

questions.question: What term commonly refers to cryptocurrencies other than Bitcoin?
questions.explanation: Altcoin is a common term for cryptocurrencies other than Bitcoin. The category does not guarantee a particular consensus mechanism or profitability.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding cryptocurrency categories and when they apply

questions.question: What term best describes an asset issued through a contract on an existing chain without creating a new independent blockchain?
questions.explanation: An asset managed under the issuance rules or smart contracts of an existing chain is generally called a token. Not every token has its own blockchain.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding cryptocurrency categories and when they apply

questions.question: What is a cryptocurrency whose name and imagery draw on internet memes or community culture commonly called?
questions.explanation: A meme coin is a cryptocurrency formed around memes or a community identity. Its name or popularity alone does not establish utility or price stability.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding cryptocurrency categories and when they apply

questions.question: What type of token is designed to grant the ability to vote on protocol governance proposals?
questions.explanation: A governance token may be used for proposals or voting under defined rules. It does not automatically represent company shares or an entitlement to guaranteed dividends.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding cryptocurrency categories and when they apply

questions.question: What term describes a token designed to pay service fees or access specific features?
questions.explanation: The term utility token focuses on functionality for using a service. Its actual scope of use must be checked against the service's implementation and terms.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding cryptocurrency categories and when they apply

questions.question: Which is the best example of an RWA token, meaning a token linked to a real-world asset?

options.text: A test coin not linked to any asset
A token designed to represent rights to a real-world bond
A backup file of a wallet's public key
A string containing a compressed block header

questions.explanation: RWA stands for real-world assets. The rights a token represents depend on asset custody and the contractual structure. Issuing a token alone does not guarantee that the underlying asset exists.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding cryptocurrency categories and when they apply

questions.question: What term refers to a digital form of central bank money issued by a central bank?
questions.explanation: CBDC stands for central bank digital currency. Its issuer differs from that of a privately issued stablecoin or Bitcoin, which is not issued by a central bank.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding cryptocurrency categories and when they apply

questions.question: What is the purpose of wrapping native BTC as a token on another chain?

options.text: To change Bitcoin's original supply cap
To use a BTC-linked asset in apps on another chain
To delete all Bitcoin mining records
To publish the recipient's private key

questions.explanation: Wrapping makes a representation linked to an underlying asset usable in another environment. Risks in the connecting structure, such as a custodian or bridge, remain separate from the risks of holding native BTC.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding cryptocurrency categories and when they apply

questions.question: What information can you mainly find in a cryptocurrency project's whitepaper?

options.text: A list of every user's actual private keys
An exchange guarantee fixing future market prices
A regulator-guaranteed commitment to repay principal
The project's explanation of its goals and technical and economic design

questions.explanation: A whitepaper explains a project's design and plans. The existence of a document must be distinguished from whether its contents have been implemented or independently verified.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding cryptocurrency categories and when they apply

questions.question: How should you interpret a future feature-release schedule in a project roadmap?

options.text: It is a listing date promised by every exchange
It is the token's future rate of return
It is a development plan that may change or be delayed
It is a past record already finalized under consensus rules

questions.explanation: A roadmap is a plan of intended future work. Actual releases must be checked separately through code, operational results, official progress updates, and other evidence.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding cryptocurrency categories and when they apply

questions.question: What is the field that analyzes token issuance, allocation, uses, and reward structures commonly called?
questions.explanation: Tokenomics concerns the economic structure through which tokens are created, allocated, and used. The price per token alone cannot reveal this structure.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding token economics and when its concepts apply

questions.question: What formula is generally used to calculate circulating market capitalization?
questions.explanation: Circulating market capitalization is calculated by multiplying the current price by circulating supply. It does not represent a total amount of cash that all holders could realize by selling at that price.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding token economics and when its concepts apply

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes circulating supply from maximum supply?

options.text: Circulating supply is the quantity currently in circulation, while maximum supply is the limit specified by the rules
The two values are always identical for every token
Circulating supply includes all future issuance, while maximum supply is today's trading volume
Both are alternative names for the token price

questions.explanation: Circulating supply and a supply cap are different concepts. Some projects may have no fixed maximum supply, and methods of counting circulating supply may differ.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding token economics and when its concepts apply

questions.question: In this question, FDV is defined as current price × maximum supply. What does FDV represent?

options.text: The cash amount that can definitely be redeemed today
The value of the entire maximum supply at the current price
A valuation using only the current circulating supply

questions.explanation: Under this definition, FDV values even the portion of maximum supply not yet in circulation at the same price. It does not guarantee that the current price will remain unchanged as future supply increases.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding token economics and when its concepts apply

questions.question: What structure restricts tokens allocated to a team so they are distributed gradually over 3 years?
questions.explanation: Vesting allows rights to tokens or withdrawable quantities to accrue gradually over time or when conditions are met. It differs from an allocation that can be used in full immediately.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding token economics and when its concepts apply

questions.question: What does a cliff period generally mean in a vesting schedule?

options.text: The point at which a private key is automatically destroyed
A period during which block propagation stops
The waiting period before the first distribution or unlock begins
The fee rate charged whenever tokens are traded

questions.explanation: A cliff is a period during which tokens are not distributed or unlocked before a specified date. The amount unlocked at that date depends on the specific agreement.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding token economics and when its concepts apply

questions.question: What is the best interpretation of a token unlock?

options.text: The price of every token has automatically risen
The blockchain has stopped verifying signatures
Existing holders' quantities have necessarily doubled
Some previously restricted tokens have become usable under specified conditions

questions.explanation: An unlock makes previously restricted tokens available for use. How much is actually sold in the market and how the price changes are separate questions.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding token economics and when its concepts apply

questions.question: What is the usual effect of a burn function that actually reduces the total supply tracked by the protocol?

options.text: It removes the specified quantity from total supply
It fixes buy prices on every exchange
It resets the entire transaction history
It automatically gives the burner the same quantity of new tokens

questions.explanation: A supply-reducing burn removes a specified quantity of tokens. A reduction in supply alone does not determine demand or the direction of the market price.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding token economics and when its concepts apply

questions.question: Why should you check the shares allocated to the team and early investors in a token allocation chart?

options.text: To understand ownership concentration and future unlock amounts
To change the number of characters in an address
To calculate the private keys for every token

questions.explanation: Allocation percentages help reveal how concentrated decision-making power or potential selling supply is among a small number of parties. Actual unlock schedules and permissions should be examined alongside the percentages.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding token economics and when its concepts apply

questions.question: Why is a coin priced at KRW 10 not necessarily more undervalued than one priced at KRW 100,000?

options.text: Because token price has no relationship to market capitalization
Because the assets have different circulating supplies and structures
Because a lower price necessarily means higher mining costs
Because every coin has the same maximum supply

questions.explanation: The price per unit can differ greatly depending on supply units. Comparing prices alone without examining circulating market capitalization and uses can misrepresent an asset's scale.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding token economics and when its concepts apply

questions.question: What role does KRW play in the trading pair BTC/KRW?

options.text: The currency in which the BTC price is quoted
A storage format for BTC private keys
A unit of BTC's maximum supply

questions.explanation: This pair indicates how many Korean won one unit of BTC trades for. The first asset is the asset being traded, and the second currency is the basis for quoting its price.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding trading basics and when they apply

questions.question: What does the best bid in an order book mean?

options.text: The lowest price among current sell orders
The highest price among current buy orders
The average execution price last month

questions.explanation: The best bid is the highest price currently offered by buyers. It differs from the last traded price because it is the price of an order that has not yet been executed.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding trading basics and when they apply

questions.question: What is the difference between a bid of KRW 990 and an ask of KRW 1,010 called?
questions.explanation: The spread is the difference between the best ask and best bid. A narrow spread alone does not guarantee enough order-book depth to absorb a large order.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding trading basics and when they apply

questions.question: Which order seeks prompt execution at currently available prices rather than specifying a price?
questions.explanation: A market order attempts execution against existing opposing orders. It may fill across several price levels, so its average execution price can differ from the displayed price.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding trading basics and when they apply

questions.question: Which order type buys only at KRW 1,000 or less per unit?

options.text: A market sell with no price limit

questions.explanation: A limit buy specifies the highest price the buyer will pay. It may not execute if no sell orders meet that condition.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding trading basics and when they apply

questions.question: An order is placed for 10 units, but only 4 trade and 6 remain. What is this state called?
questions.explanation: A partial fill means only some of the ordered quantity has actually traded. Whether the remaining quantity stays open or is canceled depends on the order conditions.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding trading basics and when they apply

questions.question: What is the key distinction between a maker and a taker?

options.text: Whether they provide resting liquidity to the order book or consume it immediately
Whether their private key is 32 bytes long
Whether they originally created the coin
Whether they have mined at least one block

questions.explanation: A maker supplies a resting order, while a taker immediately trades against an existing order. The terms do not distinguish a trader's profession or involvement in issuing a coin.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding trading basics and when they apply

questions.question: What is the difference between the expected price when submitting an order and the actual execution price commonly called?
questions.explanation: Slippage is the difference between an expected price and the actual execution price. It may result from insufficient liquidity or a price change while the order is processed.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding trading basics and when they apply

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes spot trading from trading futures contracts?

options.text: Spot trading must always use borrowed money
Settlement is possible only on a specified expiration date
Spot trading buys or sells the underlying asset itself on current terms

questions.explanation: Spot trading involves buying and selling the underlying asset. Its structure differs from trading a derivative contract based on an asset's price or another reference.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding trading basics and when they apply

questions.question: What should you check alongside a trading-volume figure?

options.text: The size of the wallet's background image
The measurement period and quantity or value units
The color of the exchange's logo
The number of letters in the coin's name

questions.explanation: Trading volume aggregates trades executed during a period. The same number can have different meanings when the time range or reference-asset units differ.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding trading basics and when they apply

questions.question: What generally increases as leverage increases?

options.text: The sensitivity of gains and losses on equity to the same price movement
The cryptographic length of a private key
The scope of principal protection provided by the blockchain

questions.explanation: Leverage creates a position larger than the trader's equity. It can magnify losses when prices move unfavorably as well as gains when they move favorably.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding market risk and when its concepts apply

questions.question: Which statement most simply describes the directional price exposure of a long position?

options.text: Price movements and profit or loss are always unrelated
All else equal, only a price decline is favorable
All else equal, a price rise is favorable

questions.explanation: A long position generally benefits from a rise in the underlying asset's price. Fees and holding costs also affect the actual net profit or loss.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding market risk and when its concepts apply

questions.question: Which statement most closely describes a typical purpose of a short position?

options.text: To gain exposure to falling prices or reduce existing exposure to rising prices

questions.explanation: A short position is positioned to benefit from falling prices. It can hedge the price risk of existing asset holdings, but carries its own risk of losses.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding market risk and when its concepts apply

questions.question: What is the process of forcibly closing a position when margin falls below the required level called?
questions.explanation: Liquidation may occur when the collateral or margin conditions required to maintain a position are no longer met. The exact thresholds and closing procedures differ between trading systems.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding market risk and when its concepts apply

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes isolated margin from cross margin?

options.text: Isolated margin applies only to spot assets, and cross margin only to NFTs
Isolated margin focuses on collateral allocated to each position, while cross margin shares collateral within a defined scope
Isolated margin always prevents losses, while cross margin always requires no collateral
Both are methods of encrypting wallet addresses

questions.explanation: Isolated and cross margin define different scopes for the collateral available to absorb losses. Details such as automatic margin additions must also be checked to understand the actual risk exposure.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding market risk and when its concepts apply

questions.question: What is the main role of funding payments in perpetual futures?

options.text: To incentivize the derivative price to move closer to the spot reference price
To issue a coin's private keys
To convert every trade into an on-chain transaction
To always guarantee traders a profit

questions.explanation: Funding creates payments between positions under the contract's rules to help adjust price deviations. Payment direction and calculation intervals may differ by product.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding market risk and when its concepts apply

questions.question: What indicator combines information from several markets to provide a reference price for cryptocurrency trading?
questions.explanation: An index price combines data from designated markets to establish a reference price. It is not necessarily equal to the latest single trade on one exchange.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding market risk and when its concepts apply

questions.question: What term describes the difference between a futures market price and the spot reference price?
questions.explanation: Basis is the difference between futures and spot prices. A price difference does not guarantee a profit when fees and funding risks are ignored.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding market risk and when its concepts apply

questions.question: When the same asset has different prices on exchanges A and B, what is needed to assess the actual arbitrage opportunity?

options.text: There is no need to check trading volume
Trade only if the two exchanges have the same address
Consider fees, deposit and withdrawal availability, and time delays together
Treat the displayed price difference as guaranteed profit

questions.explanation: A displayed price difference is not the same as profit that can actually be captured. Prices may change during transfer delays or trading restrictions.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding market risk and when its concepts apply

questions.question: What term describes a group artificially driving up a price and then selling its holdings?
questions.explanation: A pump and dump uses exaggerated promotion or coordinated trading to raise attention and prices before selling. It can leave late participants with substantial losses.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding market risk and when its concepts apply

questions.question: After buying coins on an exchange, which menu is generally needed to move them to a personal wallet?
questions.explanation: Buying changes a balance inside the exchange, while a withdrawal requests a transfer to an external address. The asset and withdrawal network may need to be selected separately.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding exchange deposits and withdrawals and their conditions

questions.question: When checking a USDT deposit address, what must match in addition to the token name?

options.text: The date the exchange account was opened
A transfer network supported by the receiving service

questions.explanation: Tokens with the same name can exist on multiple networks. Sending on a network the receiving service does not support may prevent automatic crediting or make recovery difficult.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding exchange deposits and withdrawals and their conditions

questions.question: Why does an exchange mainly require a Destination Tag for an XRP deposit?

options.text: To convert the XRP price into Korean won
To encrypt the XRP private key
To distinguish customers sharing a deposit address

questions.explanation: A tag connects a payment arriving at a shared address to a specific customer within the service. Even with the correct address, automatic crediting may be difficult if the required tag is missing.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding exchange deposits and withdrawals and their conditions

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes an exchange's withdrawal fee and the network fee of the corresponding blockchain?

options.text: Both are always zero on every network
The withdrawal fee determines the length of the private key
The service's withdrawal charge may differ from the actual on-chain cost
They are always exactly the same at every exchange

questions.explanation: Exchanges can set their own withdrawal-fee policies. Even when an exchange batches several withdrawals into one transaction, the charge per user cannot be assumed to equal the actual transaction cost.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding exchange deposits and withdrawals and their conditions

questions.question: Why might an exchange be slow to credit a deposit even after the on-chain payment is confirmed?

options.text: The block explorer is holding the balance
The private key for a valid transaction was automatically deleted
The token must have been converted into another asset
The exchange's confirmation threshold or internal processing is still pending

questions.explanation: Inclusion on the chain and crediting a customer's service balance are separate steps. Check both the service's required confirmation count and the deposit status.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding exchange deposits and withdrawals and their conditions

questions.question: Why should you check an exchange's minimum deposit amount?

options.text: Because the receiving address turns into a private key depending on the amount
Because services may have different conditions for crediting small deposits
Because the minimum deposit equals every coin's maximum supply
Because blockchains cannot record small units

questions.explanation: Even a transfer processed by the network may fall below a service's minimum deposit requirement. Actual crediting and recovery conditions must be checked in that service's guidance.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding exchange deposits and withdrawals and their conditions

questions.question: Why add a second authentication factor to exchange login?

options.text: To share the password with every employee
To add another barrier even if the password is exposed

questions.explanation: Multifactor authentication requires different kinds of verification for account access. It does not eliminate every risk, such as phishing or device theft, so authentication codes must also be protected.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding exchange security and when its concepts apply
