questions.explanation: Voting power depends on implementation rules such as token quantity, delegation, and eligibility. Voting weights and participation methods are not identical across DAOs.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about DAOs and explaining why

questions.question: Once an exchange has reviewed a token for listing, it cannot later become risky through changes to administrator permissions or declining liquidity.
questions.explanation: Asset and market conditions can change after listing. Passing a review in the past does not eliminate all subsequent operational or technical risks.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about trading support and explaining why

questions.question: An app that works well on a testnet may behave differently under actual mainnet liquidity or congestion conditions.
questions.explanation: Test environments and mainnet may differ in asset values, participants, congestion, and external integrations. Test results are only part of the necessary validation.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about test environments and explaining why

questions.question: Gas fees paid to receive reward tokens can always be excluded when calculating actual net returns.
questions.explanation: Actual costs of claiming rewards or redepositing them affect net returns. Costs can exceed rewards, especially for small amounts.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about returns and explaining why

questions.question: A high asking price for an NFT always means there are enough buy orders willing to pay that price.
questions.explanation: The price a seller asks and the price buyers are willing to pay are different. Check actual trade history and buying liquidity.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about NFTs and explaining why

questions.question: If a smart contract's name includes audited, you can conclude that a security audit has been completed even without an actual audit report.
questions.explanation: A contract name is a string its developer can choose. The actual auditor, report, code version, and findings must be checked separately.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about project evaluation and explaining why

questions.question: Before sending funds, you may need to check whether the recipient has provided a new deposit address, even if you previously saved their receiving details.
questions.explanation: Custodial services can change deposit addresses or supported networks. Compare the latest official receiving information and check whether the old address remains usable.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about user protection and explaining why

questions.question: If a project's code is public, you can additionally check whether it matches the code actually deployed.
questions.explanation: It is important to verify the correspondence between code in a public repository and the bytecode of the live contract. The existence of public code does not establish that the deployed version is identical.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about project evaluation and explaining why

questions.question: Part of a single limit order can execute immediately while the remainder waits in the order book.
questions.explanation: An order can consume some existing opposing quotes and then leave a remainder, producing both states. Fees may also differ between the immediately executed portion and the portion executed after resting.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market trading and explaining why

questions.question: If a token has no fixed maximum supply, there is no way at all to check its circulating supply or issuance rules.
questions.explanation: Having no fixed cap differs from having an unknowable supply. On-chain state and issuance rules can reveal the current quantity and how it changes.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market metrics and explaining why

questions.question: If the market price of an additional reward token falls, the displayed value-based yield may decline even when the quantity of deposited assets is unchanged.
questions.explanation: Value-based yields use both reward quantities and reward-asset prices. Value can fall even when the reward quantity is constant.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about returns and explaining why

questions.question: If no balance appears after entering a recovery phrase, the phrase must be wrong, and there is no need to check the selected network.
questions.explanation: Balances may appear differently because of supported assets, networks, derivation paths, indexing problems, or other factors. An incorrect phrase should not be assumed to be the only possible cause.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about wallet usage and explaining why

questions.question: Even without withdrawal permission, an API key with trading permission can cause harm through unwanted trades.
questions.explanation: Different permissions create different risks. Even when withdrawals are disabled, an attacker may execute unfavorable trades or alter positions.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about account security and explaining why

questions.question: Even if rewards increase the number of tokens held, a larger drop in token price can reduce their valuation in Korean won.
questions.explanation: Quantity growth and price changes are separate factors. The final valuation reflects both the quantity and the price in the relevant currency.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market risk and explaining why

questions.question: If one issuer deploys its stablecoin on multiple chains, the contract address may need to be checked separately on each chain.
questions.explanation: Even the same brand may be issued through separate contracts on different networks. Compare official supported chains and contract addresses to distinguish it from imitation tokens.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about stablecoins and explaining why

questions.question: The last traded price on a cryptocurrency exchange can differ from the current best ask in the order book.
questions.explanation: The last traded price belongs to a completed trade. If current orders change, the price available to buy now may be different.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market trading and explaining why

questions.question: A strategy that profited from past trades can later lose money if fees or market structure change.
questions.explanation: Past results arose from particular data and conditions. The same outcome may not recur if future execution conditions, costs, or competition change.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market risk and explaining why

questions.question: If a proof-of-reserves report shows a large wallet balance, every liability owed to customers has also automatically been disclosed in full.
questions.explanation: Proof that assets are held differs from proof that all liabilities have been included. A balance at one point in time alone cannot establish overall solvency.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about custody risk and explaining why

questions.question: If votes in favor exceed votes against, every DAO immediately executes the spending even if quorum or execution-delay conditions are not met.
questions.explanation: Conditions such as minimum participation and waiting periods can apply in addition to the ratio of votes for and against. The specific execution process must follow the governance rules.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about DAO operations and explaining why

questions.question: Team tokens subject to vesting remain safe forever merely because a vesting contract exists, regardless of administrators' powers to change it.
questions.explanation: Cancellation, administrator, and upgrade permissions must be checked alongside the schedule. The mere existence of a contract does not eliminate the risk of abuse of authority.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about token distribution and explaining why

questions.question: Even if a transfer address has the same 0x format, you must check whether the receiving exchange supports that network.
questions.explanation: Identical address formatting does not mean the same chain or deposit-processing route. Assets sent over the wrong network may not be credited automatically.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about deposit and withdrawal practices and explaining why

questions.question: On a DEX where liquidity pools can be created without permission, the fact that a token is traded does not establish that it has passed a separate listing review.
questions.explanation: When pool creation is open, imitation or risky tokens can also establish trading routes. Tradability must be distinguished from verification of trustworthiness.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about trading support and explaining why

questions.question: Anything called a stablecoin has the same legal structure and protections as a bank deposit everywhere in the world.
questions.explanation: Rights and protections may differ with issuance structures, usage terms, and jurisdiction. A name alone should not lead to an assumption of bank-deposit-like protection.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about stablecoins and explaining why

questions.question: A new wallet app that imports an existing account on the same network can display the balance of that same address.
questions.explanation: Balances are associated with the state of the chain, not the app's display. Viewing the same account in several apps does not duplicate assets.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about wallet usage and explaining why

questions.question: Changing an exchange password revokes every on-chain token approval previously granted to external dapps.
questions.explanation: Exchange account-security settings and smart contract approvals from an external wallet are different states. On-chain permissions must be managed separately through the relevant wallet and network.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about account security and explaining why

questions.question: If an asset's price falls only slightly below the purchase price, a leveraged position cannot suffer a large loss, so checking collateral is unnecessary.
questions.explanation: With high leverage, even a small price movement can create a large loss relative to equity. Collateral requirements and liquidation thresholds must be checked separately.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market risk and explaining why

questions.question: A mining pool operator automatically obtains private keys that allow it to send BTC arbitrarily from the personal wallets of everyone who joins the pool.
questions.explanation: Joining a pool and sharing a personal wallet's private key are separate matters. Providing a reward payout address alone does not grant spending authority over that address.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about mining economics and explaining why

questions.question: If the same coin is traded multiple times in one day, all of those executions may count toward the day's trading volume.
questions.explanation: Trading volume aggregates executed trades during a specific period. It differs from supply, which counts how many distinct coins actually exist.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market metrics and explaining why

questions.question: If a chain-data indexer updates slowly, an actually confirmed transaction may appear late in an app's list.
questions.explanation: An indexer processes chain data into a form that is easy to query. Chain confirmation, indexing, and display updates may occur at different times.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about app architecture and explaining why

questions.question: If APY is displayed higher than APR, the principal is guaranteed in Korean won regardless of a decline in the reward token's price.
questions.explanation: APY is a rate that reflects reinvestment effects, not a mechanism that guarantees asset prices. Quantity-based returns must be distinguished from gains and losses valued in a currency.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about returns and explaining why

questions.question: Increasing position size to recover a loss guarantees recovery of the principal regardless of probabilities.
questions.explanation: A larger position can also increase the size of additional losses. Increasing a position does not guarantee profit or eliminate losses that have already occurred.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market risk and explaining why

questions.question: Intermediate nodes that forward Lightning payments can set routing fees.
questions.explanation: A payment passing through several channels can be affected by forwarding nodes' fee policies. Being an off-chain payment does not mean it is always free.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about Lightning and explaining why

questions.question: Both a stablecoin issuer's published reserves and its actual redemption-eligibility conditions are worth examining.
questions.explanation: Who can redeem, when, and how matters as well as the composition of reserves. Reserve disclosures alone cannot establish that an individual can redeem immediately.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about stablecoins and explaining why

questions.question: Buying coins on an exchange automatically transfers the on-chain private keys held by that exchange to the buyer.
questions.explanation: A custodial exchange usually manages private keys and displays an internal balance to the user. Simply buying differs from withdrawing to a personal wallet.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about deposit and withdrawal practices and explaining why

questions.question: Anyone who knows your wallet's public transaction history accurately must be an official customer-support employee.
questions.explanation: Anyone can look up transaction history on a public chain. Knowing some public information does not authenticate someone as an authorized support representative.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about user protection and explaining why

questions.question: Even if the unlock date for investors' tokens is known, how much is actually sold that day is a separate decision.
questions.explanation: An unlock makes tokens available for use. Holding them, using them for another purpose, or selling them is a subsequent choice by their holders.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about token distribution and explaining why

questions.question: The KRW valuation displayed in a wallet is a single value directly recorded by blockchain consensus for every exchange.
questions.explanation: Displayed valuations are often calculated using price data and exchange rates selected by the app. On-chain token quantities and external currency-price information are distinct.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about app architecture and explaining why

questions.question: If authority to change an NFT's metadata remains, its image reference can be changed later.
questions.explanation: A token identifier and the authority to modify metadata are separate properties. Check whether the structure allows changes and who holds that authority.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about NFT metadata and explaining why

questions.question: Selling a liquid staking token on an exchange means all underlying validators have immediately exited.
questions.explanation: Selling the token in a market changes the holder of the associated rights. It does not simultaneously cause underlying validators to exit or assets to be redeemed.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about staking and explaining why

questions.question: A pause function in a smart contract can help respond to emergencies while also creating dependence on an administrator.
questions.explanation: Pause authority can help limit the spread of an incident. At the same time, operational risks depend on who may pause or resume activity and under what conditions.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about project evaluation and explaining why

questions.question: Once a bridge exists between chains, every type of token can automatically be transferred in both directions without separate support.
questions.explanation: A bridge supports defined assets, directions, and verification methods. The existence of a connection and support for every asset are separate conditions.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about interoperability and explaining why

questions.question: Even when an NFT's image is stored on an external server, blockchain consensus automatically takes responsibility for operating that server forever.
questions.explanation: Recording a file reference on a blockchain does not make operation and storage of an external server part of the blockchain. If the server stops, the content may become unreadable.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about NFT metadata and explaining why

questions.question: Any number labeled as an annual yield is guaranteed to be paid regardless of the deposit period or product conditions.
questions.explanation: A displayed rate may annualize a variable rate or a current estimate. Actual payment conditions and costs must be checked.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market risk and explaining why

questions.question: Even if coins A and B have the same unit price, their circulating market capitalizations can differ if their circulating supplies differ.
questions.explanation: Market capitalization uses circulating supply as well as price. An identical unit price does not imply the same asset scale.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market metrics and explaining why

questions.question: Because Lightning uses payment channels, it never requires a Bitcoin on-chain transaction, no matter what failure occurs.
questions.explanation: On-chain transactions may be used to open or close channels and resolve disputes. Lightning is not a payment system entirely independent of the underlying chain.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about Lightning and explaining why

questions.question: Finding a token's page on a block explorer proves that the token is included in an exchange's supported deposit list.
questions.explanation: A token's on-chain existence and an exchange's support policy are different matters. Sending an unsupported asset may prevent the service from crediting it to the balance.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about deposit and withdrawal practices and explaining why

questions.question: At a Bitcoin halving, the rules also cut the transaction fee of every transaction to exactly half.
questions.explanation: A halving reduces the newly issued subsidy. Transaction fees offered by users vary with network demand and transaction conditions.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about mining economics and explaining why

questions.question: Even if a very small last trade moves the price sharply, not every holder can necessarily cash out at that price.
questions.explanation: Prices must be interpreted alongside executable market depth. In a thin market, a large sell order may consume orders at several lower price levels.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market trading and explaining why

questions.question: A DAO can define different rules for who may create proposals and who may execute transfers of treasury assets.
questions.explanation: Proposal creation, voting, and execution can be separate permission stages. Calling something a DAO does not mean everyone has every permission.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about DAOs and explaining why

questions.question: Publishing a service's wallet addresses can help users check some of its on-chain balances.
questions.explanation: Public addresses can be used to look up asset balances. However, additional information is needed to assess total liabilities and whether assets are encumbered as collateral.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about custody risk and explaining why

questions.question: A request to send more assets upfront in exchange for recovering funds lost to a previous transfer scam may itself be another scam.
questions.explanation: Some schemes exploit victims by requesting additional payments as supposed recovery fees. The legitimacy of a recovery service must be checked independently of the original loss.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about user protection and explaining why

questions.question: When using a DeFi service, the operator of the web interface and the holder of smart contract administrator permissions may be different parties.
questions.explanation: Roles such as interface operation, contract deployment and administration, and data provision can be separate. Distinguish each controlling party and the impact of its failure.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about DeFi risks and explaining why

questions.question: If a coin once reached a high of KRW 100,000, it is guaranteed to trade at KRW 100,000 again in the future.
questions.explanation: A historical high is a trading price observed in the past. Changes in supply, demand, and market conditions mean it does not guarantee a future recovery.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market metrics and explaining why

questions.question: When a celebrity promotes a coin, that endorsement alone technically verifies the safety of its smart contracts.
questions.explanation: Promotion and security verification are different activities. Safety cannot be concluded without evidence such as code reviews, operational permissions, and audit scope.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about project evaluation and explaining why

questions.question: If the screen showed KRW 100 immediately before you pressed Market Buy, the entire order must execute at KRW 100.
questions.explanation: A market order may execute sequentially against available sell orders. If there is insufficient volume or quotes change, the average execution price will differ from KRW 100.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market trading and explaining why

questions.question: To hold XRP, a user must personally participate in proof-of-work mining to create that XRP.
questions.explanation: The XRP Ledger does not use Bitcoin-style proof-of-work mining. Users can hold XRP by receiving it from other holders, among other methods.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about the XRP Ledger and explaining why

questions.question: Every Lightning invoice remains valid indefinitely, and an invoice already paid can be paid repeatedly without limit under the same conditions.
questions.explanation: Invoices can have expiration conditions and usage conditions associated with payment identifiers. Reusing an old invoice should not be assumed to provide a general-purpose unlimited payment method.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about Lightning and explaining why

questions.question: Because DeFi runs through smart contracts, lending and liquidation always operate as safely as usual even if the price feed they use stops.
questions.explanation: Errors or interruptions in external price information affect collateral valuations and liquidation decisions. Automatic execution does not eliminate the need for trustworthy input data.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about DeFi risks and explaining why

questions.question: Token ownership and copyright or commercial-use permission for the associated work may be separate matters.
questions.explanation: An NFT transfer changes the token ownership record. Specific usage rights for the work may be determined by a separate license or agreement.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about NFT rights and explaining why

questions.question: An increase in stablecoin issuance alone guarantees a profit for everyone who bought that token.
questions.explanation: Issuance changes supply; it does not determine investment profit or loss. Prices, redemption conditions, costs, and usage circumstances must be considered separately.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about stablecoins and explaining why

questions.question: A read-only API secret key cannot move assets, so publishing it in a public repository cannot expose balance information.
questions.explanation: Read permission alone may reveal sensitive information, such as balances or transaction histories. Lacking write permission does not mean the key is safe to publish.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about account security and explaining why

questions.question: Annualizing rewards from a product held for one day may include an assumption that those conditions will continue.
questions.explanation: Displaying short-term rewards on an annual basis makes comparison easier, but sustainability must be checked separately. It does not mean a full year's rewards have already been determined.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about returns and explaining why

questions.question: Every service with staking in its name earns returns exclusively from consensus-validation rewards.
questions.explanation: Some services may use the same label for lending or other asset-management activities. Check where funds are actually used and where rewards come from.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about staking and explaining why

questions.question: A recovery phrase written on paper is not connected to the internet, so there is no need to protect it from photography or theft.
questions.explanation: Offline media can still be copied, photographed, or lost. Reducing online exposure and controlling physical access are separate matters.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about wallet usage and explaining why

questions.question: Canceling a sell order automatically returns quantities that have already been executed and sold.
questions.explanation: Cancellation generally applies to the remaining unfilled quantity. A cancellation request alone does not reverse trades that have already occurred.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market trading and explaining why

questions.question: A developer can create a local chain separately from a public testnet.
questions.explanation: A local development network tests chain execution and state in a private environment. It does not reproduce every participation condition of a public network.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about test environments and explaining why

questions.question: Existing holders' token quantities may stay unchanged even when total supply increases.
questions.explanation: Issuing new tokens to other accounts may leave existing holders' quantities unchanged. However, their share of total supply can decrease.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about market metrics and explaining why

questions.question: If every image in an NFT collection is publicly available, there is no need to further check the relationship between the token issuer and the original creator.
questions.explanation: Public availability of images does not prove legitimate issuance rights or the original creator's consent. The project, creator, and rights conditions must be verified separately.
questions.learningObjective: Evaluating statements about NFT rights and explaining why

questions.question: How do you send only part of the value of a single Bitcoin UTXO to someone?

options.text: Spend the entire UTXO as an input and create a change output
Reduce only the existing amount field of that UTXO by the amount sent
Append a new output for the same amount without spending the UTXO
Mark part of the UTXO as spent and the remainder as unspent

questions.explanation: A UTXO is consumed in full when it is spent as an input. To receive the amount left after the payment, allocate it to a new change output.
questions.learningObjective: UTXO spending and the structure of change

questions.question: A Bitcoin transaction has several outputs. What must a later transaction reference to spend a specific output?

options.text: The recipient address and output amount of the previous transaction
The txid and sender address of the previous transaction
Only the height of the previous block and the transaction's position
The txid of the previous transaction and the index of that output

questions.explanation: An input's outpoint identifies a specific UTXO using a txid and an output index. The txid alone cannot distinguish multiple outputs in the same transaction.
questions.learningObjective: Precisely identifying the output to spend

questions.question: You use UTXOs worth 80,000 sat and 40,000 sat to send 90,000 sat, with a fee of 3,000 sat. How much change do you receive?
questions.explanation: Subtracting the payment of 90,000 sat and the fee of 3,000 sat from the total input of 120,000 sat leaves 27,000 sat in change.
questions.learningObjective: Calculating change using input-output conservation

questions.question: A fully signed transaction has a virtual size of 175 vB, and the fee rate is 8 sat/vB. What is the total fee?
questions.explanation: The total fee is the virtual size multiplied by the fee rate: 175×8=1,400 sat. A vB is a unit of size that accounts for SegWit weighting.
questions.learningObjective: Calculating fees from virtual size

questions.question: Two different transactions attempt to spend the same UTXO. If both have valid signatures, what can happen on a single valid chain?

options.text: Both can spend the UTXO if both signatures are valid
Only one of them can spend the UTXO
The same UTXO can be spent again if the transactions are in different blocks
Both can spend it together if their fee rates are equal

questions.explanation: Validation checks not only signatures but also whether an input remains unspent. A transaction that reuses an already spent UTXO cannot coexist with the earlier spend on a valid chain.
questions.learningObjective: Identifying conflicting transactions and double spending

questions.question: Two candidate Bitcoin chains satisfy all consensus rules but have different amounts of cumulative work. Which criterion does a node use to choose its preferred chain?

options.text: The chain with more cumulative work
Only the chain relayed by more peers
The chain with a larger total transaction value
Only the chain with a greater block height

questions.explanation: Bitcoin compares the cumulative work of candidate chains that have passed validation. The number of transactions or the amount transferred is not the criterion.
questions.learningObjective: Comparing chains by cumulative work

questions.question: A transaction is included in the block at height 100, and the current canonical chain tip is at height 103. Counting the inclusion block as the first confirmation, how many confirmations does it have?
questions.explanation: Confirmations equal current height−inclusion height+1, so 103−100+1=4. The count must be recalculated if the chain reorganizes.
questions.learningObjective: Calculating confirmations from block heights

questions.question: An SPV wallet checks a transaction and its Merkle path against the Merkle root in a block header. What does this procedure directly verify?

options.text: The transaction is included in the transaction set committed to by that header
The transaction parties have completed real-name verification
The block can never be reorganized out of the chain
All transaction inputs in the block are fully valid

questions.explanation: A Merkle path verifies inclusion. Unlike a full node, SPV does not independently re-execute all transaction consensus rules.
questions.learningObjective: Interpreting the scope of an SPV proof

questions.question: In a complete binary Merkle tree with 8 leaves, an inclusion proof sends the sibling hash at each level. How many sibling hashes are needed for one leaf?
questions.explanation: The three levels, 8→4→2→1, require one sibling hash each. The leaf and root themselves are not included in the sibling-hash count.
questions.learningObjective: Calculating path length in a balanced Merkle tree

questions.question: A wallet requires signatures from 2 of 3 independently stored keys, and one key has been lost. If the other keys and the necessary wallet information are available, what can be done?

options.text: The existing spending condition automatically changes to 1-of-2
Spending is impossible because all three original keys are required
Spending is possible only if the first two registered keys remain
The two remaining keys can satisfy the spending condition

questions.explanation: A 2-of-3 condition requires two valid signatures. Losing one key does not prevent the condition from being satisfied if the other two can still be used.
questions.learningObjective: Assessing multisignature availability

questions.question: A merchant has only confirmed that a Bitcoin transaction was broadcast to the network. How should the merchant interpret it when processing the payment?

options.text: All nodes are guaranteed to store the same transaction
It is a payment request whose inclusion in a block is not yet confirmed
Its input UTXOs are locked across the entire network
Block validation and payment finalization are already complete

questions.explanation: Broadcasting is different from block inclusion. An unconfirmed transaction can be affected by conflicting transactions and node policies.
questions.learningObjective: Handling unconfirmed transactions as payments

questions.question: A chain reorganization removes the block containing a deposit transaction from the canonical chain. What should the payment server do?

options.text: Keep the existing confirmation count if the txid has not changed
Query only the transaction fee again and keep the deposit confirmed
Recheck transaction inclusion and confirmations against the canonical chain
Increase confirmations using only elapsed time from the originally recorded block height

questions.explanation: The server must check whether the transaction is included in another canonical block, remains unconfirmed, or conflicts with another transaction. Changes in block ancestry must be reflected in the deposit status.
questions.learningObjective: Adjusting payment records after a reorganization

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares spending conditions for a UTXO received in an ordinary payment and a coinbase output created as a block reward?

options.text: Coinbase outputs have a separate maturity waiting rule
Only ordinary payment outputs have a separate maturity waiting rule
Both types can always be spent immediately after inclusion in a block
Even the block producer can never spend a coinbase output

questions.explanation: Coinbase outputs can be spent only after meeting the maturity condition set by consensus rules. They must be distinguished from ordinary transaction outputs.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding coinbase output maturity

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the txid and wtxid of a SegWit transaction?

options.text: The wtxid is based on serialization that includes witness data
The txid also always uses the same serialization including witness data
The wtxid hashes only the header of the block containing the transaction
The txid is a separate hash of only the witness data

questions.explanation: For SegWit transactions, the txid uses a format excluding witness data, while the wtxid uses a format that includes it.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing SegWit identifiers and witness data

questions.question: Two transactions have the same output structure and input type. Transaction A uses 1 input and B uses 10 inputs. At the same sat/vB fee rate, what is generally true?

options.text: More inputs automatically exempt the transaction from all fees
Equal payment amounts necessarily mean equal total fees
The number of inputs does not affect the serialized transaction size
B has a larger virtual size and therefore a higher total fee

questions.explanation: Each input needs a reference to the previous output and data proving that it can be spent. Other things being equal, more inputs increase transaction size and fees.
questions.learningObjective: Comparing input counts and transaction fees

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a Bitcoin full node that uses pruning?

options.text: It stores only addresses and does not even store block headers
It is a dedicated device that validates only blocks it mined itself
It is a wallet that performs no consensus-rule validation
It can delete some old block files after validating the blocks

questions.explanation: Pruning is a disk-storage policy. Deleting some historical block files is different from not performing full validation.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing pruning from validation capability

questions.question: You want an accounting server to have information for viewing transactions without giving it spending authority. Which setup is appropriate?

options.text: Use a watch-only wallet based on public information
Only disable automatic payments in a wallet that can sign
Store the private key on the server and hide the Send button
Store the seed and its decryption password together on the same server

questions.explanation: A watch-only wallet tracks transactions using addresses or extended public keys. Without private keys, it cannot create signatures that spend the funds.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding watch-only wallets

questions.question: What can a server holding only a BIP-32 extended public key do along a typical non-hardened derivation path?

options.text: Recover the same spending authority as the extended private key
Derive child private keys and sign spending transactions
Compute hardened child public keys using public derivation alone
Derive child public keys to generate receiving addresses

questions.explanation: An extended public key can derive non-hardened child public keys. It does not provide the secret-key authority required for hardened derivation or spending signatures.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding the derivation scope of extended public keys

questions.question: The BIP-39 recovery phrase is correct, but a different passphrase is entered. What result should you expect?

options.text: The passphrase is used only as a display account name, so addresses stay the same
The same seed is generated and only the wallet screen's unlock password changes
The recovery phrase checksum necessarily fails and seed generation stops
A different seed is generated and a different wallet may appear

questions.explanation: BIP-39 seed generation uses both the recovery phrase and the passphrase. A different passphrase can generate a different valid seed.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding how BIP-39 passphrases affect recovery

questions.question: The recipient address shown on a computer differs from the one shown on a hardware wallet. What should you do before signing?

options.text: Proceed because hardware signing does not protect the recipient address
Stop signing and check the transaction details on the device's screen
Sign and broadcast first, then check the address only in a transaction lookup
Ignore the device-screen difference if the computer shows the intended address

questions.explanation: Protecting the private key does not prevent funds from moving if you sign a payment to the wrong recipient. Check the actual content to be signed on the independent device screen.
questions.learningObjective: Checking transaction details on a hardware wallet

questions.question: An ordinary EOA, with no code delegation or other nonce changes, has a next transaction nonce of 7. If only a transaction with nonce 8 is submitted from that account, what generally happens?

options.text: It executes by skipping nonce 7 as long as a fee is paid
The recipient sets the nonce, so it has no relation to execution order
Nonce 8 cannot execute before nonce 7 is processed
Receiving nonce 8 immediately changes the account nonce to 9

questions.explanation: Ordinary transactions from the same account execute sequentially according to its nonce. A gap in earlier nonces can leave later transactions waiting.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding account nonce order and queued transactions

questions.question: An ordinary execution transaction uses 50,000 gas at an effective gas price of 20 gwei. With no additional costs, what is its execution fee?
questions.learningObjective: Calculating costs from gas used and effective gas price

questions.question: For an ordinary EIP-1559 transaction, the base fee is 30 gwei, the maximum priority fee is 3 gwei, and maxFeePerGas is 50 gwei. What is the effective gas price?
questions.explanation: The effective gas price is min(maxFeePerGas, base fee+maximum priority fee). Here, min(50,33)=33 gwei.
questions.learningObjective: Calculating the EIP-1559 effective gas price

questions.question: A transaction's gas limit is set comfortably above the amount required for execution. Which statement is correct if execution finishes successfully?

options.text: The unused gas limit is automatically carried over as the next transaction's execution limit
Increasing the gas limit increases the gas cost of each identical operation proportionally
Even successful execution always charges the entire specified gas limit as consumed
The charge is based on actual billable usage, not the entire gas limit

questions.explanation: The gas limit is the upper bound allowed for execution. Unused gas is not all charged as though it were consumed.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing the gas limit from actual usage

questions.question: A contract-call transaction is included in a block but reverts at the top level. What is the most accurate result?

options.text: State changes remain, and only the transaction hash is deleted
All contract changes remain because the transaction entered a block
Execution state changes are rolled back, but the cost of gas used remains
A revert makes all gas used during execution free

questions.explanation: A top-level revert cancels the state changes of that execution. Gas spent on operations already executed is not refunded.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding state and cost after a top-level execution failure

questions.question: An app executes a contract function using eth_call and receives a result. What kind of call is this?

options.text: It restores the contract's current state to the state of the specified historical block
It simulates execution against the specified state without changing canonical chain state
It writes the return value to a new block and permanently updates contract state
It broadcasts an unconfirmed transaction and waits for inclusion in the next block

questions.explanation: eth_call is an RPC for querying an execution result on a node. Recording actual state changes requires a separate valid transaction.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing eth_call from state-changing transactions

questions.question: An app must repeatedly query account balances at a specific block height far in the past via RPC. What capability must the node directly support?

options.text: Querying only the current state at the latest block
Querying only block-header heights and hashes
Querying the historical state at that block
Querying only lists of historical transaction hashes

questions.explanation: Holding historical block data is different from supporting state queries at arbitrary historical points. Check how the node stores data and the historical-state range it serves.
questions.learningObjective: Identifying node data needed for historical-state queries

questions.question: A transaction has a value of 0, but its data contains an ERC-20 transfer call. What is a possible interpretation?

options.text: ERC-20 transfers ignore data and read only value
Zero ETH transferred means the token ledger cannot change either
The contract can change token balances without directly transferring ETH
value contains the token amount, while data contains the ETH amount

questions.explanation: value is the amount of ETH directly delivered by the transaction. ERC-20 transfer amounts and recipients are passed in contract-call data, which can update the token ledger.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing ETH transaction value from token transfers

questions.question: Using ordinary calls, an EOA calls contract A, and A calls contract B. Who is msg.sender inside B?
questions.explanation: For an ordinary CALL, msg.sender is the immediate sender of the current call. Distinguish the original transaction sender from the caller between contracts.
questions.learningObjective: Interpreting msg.sender across call layers

questions.question: A user uses the same 0x address on different EVM networks. How should a balance-viewing app be designed?

options.text: Query balances using both the chain ID and the address
Treat token contracts at the same address as the same asset on every chain
Assume that matching addresses automatically share balances and nonces across networks
Determine the network from the address's 0x prefix alone

questions.explanation: Different chains have separate state even if they share an address format or an identical address. Identify both the network and the address.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing network-specific state for the same address

questions.question: A Solidity state array is copied into a memory array, and an element of the copy is changed. If the copy is not assigned back to storage, what happens?

options.text: Changing a memory element immediately changes the original storage element
The memory copy is automatically synchronized to storage when the function ends
Changing the copy alone does not change the original state array
Changing any element of an array copied to memory always reverts

questions.explanation: Assignment from storage to memory creates an independent copy. Persisting changes made in memory requires separate code that writes them into state.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing memory copies from storage references

questions.question: A view function is called during the execution of another state-changing transaction. Which gas statement is correct?

options.text: Its operations consume gas even though it does not write state
A view call is excluded from the enclosing transaction's gas accounting
The view modifier makes all on-chain reads and operations cost zero
All gas for a view call is refunded if its return value is unused

questions.explanation: view indicates a restriction on state changes. Reads and computation during on-chain execution still use gas and must be distinguished from eth_call queries.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding the on-chain execution cost of view functions

questions.question: What is the main reason to declare the depositor address as indexed in a deposit event?

options.text: To automatically make it a persistent state variable that the contract can read directly
To automatically turn the event into a contract function for searching past logs
To automatically grant that address permission to withdraw the deposit
To efficiently find events for that address using log topics

questions.explanation: Indexed parameters are included in event topics and used for log filtering. They do not grant permissions or keep information secret.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding the search purpose of indexed fields

questions.question: A contract must directly check cumulative past deposits during a later execution. Which storage design is appropriate?

options.text: Record only events and have the contract search its own historical logs directly
Record the cumulative amount in a state variable the contract can read
Trust a frontend's cached number as the contract's cumulative amount without validation
Assume memory values from the previous call persist into the next call

questions.explanation: Event logs are useful for external searches, but they are not a state store that contracts can directly query for past logs. Values needed for later on-chain decisions should be held in readable state.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing logs from on-chain queryable state

questions.question: A contract should allow only an administrator to change the fee rate. Which control is appropriate?

options.text: Write 'administrator only' in a source-code comment
Check the caller's authorization inside the update function
Show the button only on the administrator screen and omit contract checks
Only prefix the function name with admin

questions.explanation: Frontend restrictions do not prevent direct contract calls. Authorization conditions must be enforced when the contract executes.
questions.learningObjective: Locating and enforcing authorization checks

questions.question: When a withdrawal function sends funds to an external recipient, which basic execution order reduces reentrancy risk?

options.text: External call → external call → authorization check last
External call → internal balance check → condition checks
Check conditions → update internal balances → external call
Emit event → external call → skip balance updates

questions.explanation: Checks-Effects-Interactions checks conditions first, applies internal state changes, and then transfers control externally. The overall call flow still requires additional review.
questions.learningObjective: Ordering execution to defend against reentrancy

questions.question: Proxy P performs a delegatecall to implementation contract I. Which storage is used when I's code writes state?

options.text: The storage of both P and I simultaneously
The storage of the original transaction-sending EOA

questions.explanation: delegatecall executes the target's code in the caller's context. The proxy and implementation code therefore need compatible storage layouts.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding the storage context of delegatecall

questions.question: What are the first 4 bytes of calldata used for in a typical Solidity ABI function call?

options.text: The byte length of all ABI-encoded arguments
The byte length of all data the function will return
A shared code identifying the type of the first parameter
A selector obtained from the hash of the function signature

questions.explanation: A typical function selector is the first 4 bytes of the Keccak-256 hash of the canonical function signature. The following data contains arguments encoded according to ABI rules.
questions.learningObjective: Identifying function selectors and ABI calls

questions.question: You query an address key that has never been set in a Solidity mapping(address => uint256). What is the default result?

options.text: null is returned instead of an integer
The value most recently set for another address

questions.explanation: An unset mapping key returns the value type's default. For uint256, that default is 0, so a separate existence indicator may be necessary.
questions.learningObjective: Querying unset mapping keys

questions.question: A Solidity contract has both receive() external payable and a payable fallback. Which runs first when ETH is sent with empty calldata?
questions.explanation: For a call with empty calldata, receive is selected if it exists. The fallback handles other unmatched calls and similar cases.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding the ETH-receiving path for empty calldata

questions.question: An ERC-20 token has decimals set to 6 and a raw balance of 1,250,000. What amount should be displayed?
questions.explanation: The display amount is the raw integer balance divided by 10 to the power of decimals: 1,250,000÷1,000,000=1.25.
questions.learningObjective: Calculating display amounts using decimals

questions.question: For a standard ERC-20 token, a user successfully calls approve(100) for a spender. What does this call itself do?

options.text: Set the allowance that the spender may use
Immediately transfer 100 tokens to the spender
Lock 100 tokens so the owner cannot transfer them directly
Transfer ownership first and reverse that transfer in transferFrom

questions.explanation: approve sets the allowance. Moving tokens requires a separate operation such as transferFrom.
questions.learningObjective: Identifying the state changed by approve

questions.question: For a standard ERC-20 token, a user has a balance of 60, and a spender has a remaining allowance of 100. What is the issue if the spender tries to transferFrom 80?

options.text: Deducting the shortfall from the allowance lets a balance of 60 fund a transfer of 80
The allowance of 100 automatically replenishes the missing balance
The transfer automatically partially succeeds for the available balance of 60
The allowance is sufficient, but the user's balance is insufficient

questions.explanation: Spending approval does not create new tokens. transferFrom requires both the necessary approval and an actually available balance.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding allowance and actual balance requirements

questions.question: A call to an external ERC-20 contract does not revert, but transfer returns false. What should the calling app do?

options.text: Interpret false as a transfer amount of 0 and treat the call as successful
Ignore false and treat the call as successful if the allowance was sufficient
Check the return value and handle the failed transfer
Always treat the transfer as successful because the call did not revert

questions.explanation: The ERC-20 specification states that callers must handle a false return value. A call not reverting is not enough to assume that the transfer succeeded.
questions.learningObjective: Handling ERC-20 return values

questions.question: Two ERC-20 contracts on the same network use the symbol ABC. How should an app distinguish the assets?

options.text: Only by the combination of name and symbol
By the current token holder's address

questions.explanation: Different contracts can share names and symbols. On the same network, contract addresses distinguish token ledgers.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing token display names from contract identity

questions.question: ERC-721 contracts A and B on the same chain both issue tokenId 7. How should the two assets be distinguished?

options.text: Use only the contract address and omit tokenId
Use only the owner address and tokenId
Use the contract address together with tokenId

questions.explanation: An ERC-721 tokenId identifies a token within its contract. When multiple chains are involved, include a chain identifier as well.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding contract-scoped NFT identity

questions.question: What additional check does ERC-721 safeTransferFrom perform for a contract recipient compared with ordinary transferFrom?

options.text: Whether the recipient contract directly implements ownerOf
Whether the recipient contract has sufficient ERC-20 allowance
Whether the previous owner's token-specific approval remains after transfer
Whether the recipient properly handles the required NFT-receiving callback

questions.explanation: If the recipient is a contract, its onERC721Received response is checked. This reduces the risk of sending an NFT to a contract that cannot handle receiving it.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding recipient checks in ERC-721 safe transfers

questions.question: An ERC-721 NFT has a token-specific approved address. What happens to that approval when the NFT is successfully transferred to a different owner?

options.text: It expands into approval to manage all NFTs of the new owner
It is cleared during the transfer
It is automatically replaced with the new owner's address
It remains unchanged until the new owner revokes it

questions.explanation: ERC-721 resets the token-specific approval on transfer. This prevents a new owner from inheriting unwanted permissions granted by the previous owner.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding ERC-721 token-specific approval after ownership changes

questions.question: An ERC-721 tokenURI points to an external image and description. What can you conclude from this?

options.text: Even an external URI is permanently immutable if the token is ERC-721
There is a metadata reference, and the actual storage location must be checked separately
The presence of tokenURI proves that the entire image is in contract storage
Once tokenURI is returned, no one needs to preserve the external file

questions.explanation: tokenURI is a reference for accessing metadata. The storage method and updateability of the referenced content must be checked separately.
questions.learningObjective: Identifying where NFT metadata is stored

questions.question: You want to transfer 10 units of item ID 5 and 3 units of item ID 8 from one game contract in a single operation. Which ERC-1155 function is appropriate?

options.text: Pass an array of IDs and an array of amounts to safeBatchTransferFrom
Combine the quantities for IDs 5 and 8 and transfer everything as ID 5
Pass the ID array directly into the single-ID argument of safeTransferFrom
Separate safeTransferFrom calls for each ID are the standard's only method

questions.explanation: ERC-1155 provides a batch-transfer interface that specifies multiple IDs and their respective amounts in a single call.
questions.learningObjective: Transferring multiple token types in an ERC-1155 batch

questions.question: You want one ERC-1155 contract to manage both gold coins and limited-edition equipment. Which statement is consistent with the standard?

options.text: Each ID can represent a different supply and type of asset
Every ERC-1155 ID must have a supply of exactly 1
Different IDs always require different contract addresses
All IDs in a contract must have the same total supply

questions.explanation: ERC-1155 manages multiple token types in one contract. Depending on the implementation and supply policy, it can represent both fungible and unique assets.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding asset types for ERC-1155 IDs

questions.question: You grant setApprovalForAll(operator, true) in ERC-1155. What is the basic scope of this approval?

options.text: Direct withdrawal authority over the owner's ETH on every chain
Read access to the single token ID visible on the screen when called
Permission for the owner to use the operator's tokens
Authority to manage the owner's various token IDs within that contract

questions.explanation: Operator approval permits transfers of the owner's tokens within the specified ERC-1155 contract. It differs from a call approving only one ID.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding the scope of ERC-1155 operator approval

questions.question: You want to check whether a contract reports support for a particular standard interface. Which ERC-165 function is used?
questions.explanation: Pass an interface ID to supportsInterface to query support. A positive support response does not by itself verify the safety of the entire implementation.
questions.learningObjective: Querying supported interfaces with ERC-165

questions.question: For a token supporting ERC-2612 permit, an owner signs an approval message. What can happen next?

options.text: Creating the signature immediately updates the on-chain allowance
A third party submits the signature to execute the owner's allowance setting
A valid signature makes deadline and nonce checks unnecessary
permit can execute only in a transaction sent directly by the owner

questions.explanation: permit allows approvals to be set using a valid signature. Execution requires checks such as the nonce and deadline, and the submitting transaction still has a cost.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding the signature-based permit approval flow

questions.question: An app needs to verify a smart contract wallet's signature. Which approach follows ERC-1271?

options.text: Permanently cache the original owner's signature result and keep applying it
Check the result of the wallet contract's isValidSignature
Check only whether recovering an EOA signer produces the contract address
Accept the contract deployer's EOA signature regardless of the current wallet policy

questions.explanation: Contract wallets can determine signature validity using their own rules. ERC-1271 provides a standard interface for querying that decision.
questions.learningObjective: Verifying smart contract wallet signatures

questions.question: Ignoring fees and rounding, an x×y=k pool holds 100 X and 10,000 Y. If you add 25 X to receive Y, how much Y do you receive?
questions.explanation: k=1,000,000, and X after the swap is 125. The remaining Y is 1,000,000÷125=8,000, so the amount received is 2,000 Y.
questions.learningObjective: Calculating swap amounts in a constant-product pool

questions.question: Constant-product pools A and B hold the same two assets in the same ratio. B has 10 times A's reserves. When swapping the same input amount, what is generally true?

options.text: The trade itself causes less price impact in B
B has exactly 10 times greater price impact
Only A's price changes, while B's price stays fixed
A and B have identical price impact regardless of reserves

questions.explanation: Other things being equal, price impact decreases when the trade is smaller relative to the pool. Deeper liquidity softens the effect of large trades.
questions.learningObjective: Relating trade size relative to a pool to price impact

questions.question: In a pool with proportional redemption, an LP redeems their entire 10% share. Reserves are 500 A and 2,000 B, with no special token behavior or extra costs. What is withdrawn?
questions.explanation: Under proportional redemption, apply 10% to each reserve. An LP share does not guarantee the return of the fixed quantities originally deposited.
questions.learningObjective: Calculating withdrawals from an LP share

questions.question: A Uniswap v2-style pool holds 100 A and 10,000 B. To add liquidity at the current ratio, how much B must accompany 2 A?
questions.explanation: The current reserve ratio is 100 B per A. Maintaining that ratio requires 200 B alongside 2 A.
questions.learningObjective: Calculating deposit ratios for an existing pool

questions.question: An AMM price becomes much lower than the external market price. What effect does arbitrage generally have when it remains profitable after costs?

options.text: It forces the quantities of the pool's two reserves to become equal
More trading necessarily increases the price gap between the markets
It changes the pool's reserve ratio in a direction that narrows the price gap
It permanently fixes the pool price without referring to external prices

questions.explanation: Arbitrageurs have an incentive to buy where an asset is cheaper and sell where it is more expensive. As AMM reserves change, the gap from the external price can narrow.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding external price gaps and AMM arbitrage

questions.question: When explaining impermanent loss in an AMM, what alternative is normally used for comparison?

options.text: Fixing only the initial token quantities as a cash amount
Buying only the other asset that rose most during the period
The returns of an imaginary pool that issues no LP tokens
Simply holding the same initial assets without depositing them in the pool

questions.explanation: Impermanent loss is the value difference between providing liquidity and simply holding the initial assets. It is distinct from overall profit or loss including fee income.
questions.learningObjective: Identifying the benchmark for liquidity-provision returns

questions.question: The current price moves outside a concentrated-liquidity position's selected range. What is the state of a typical Uniswap v3-style position?

options.text: It exclusively receives all trading fees from the entire pool
It is automatically liquidated and its ownership disappears
It provides no active liquidity for current swaps and earns no fees from them
It instantly returns to the originally deposited ratio of the two assets

questions.explanation: A position's liquidity is active only within its selected range. Outside that range, its asset composition may become one-sided and fee earnings stop.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding the effects of leaving a concentrated-liquidity range

questions.question: You set a minimum amount received by applying a simple 2% slippage tolerance to an expected output of 100 tokens. Ignoring rounding, what is the minimum?
questions.explanation: The minimum amount is 100×(1−0.02)=98. The contract must enforce this condition to reject execution worse than the limit.
questions.learningObjective: Calculating a minimum output from slippage tolerance

questions.question: A flash swap's repayment check fails, and no enclosing call catches the revert. What happens to the top-level transaction?

options.text: Only the final repayment is canceled, and assets received earlier remain
The entire transaction reverts, including intermediate asset transfers
The pool absorbs the repayment shortfall from its reserves and the call succeeds
It succeeds if the next transaction in the same block is expected to repay

questions.explanation: If the repayment failure propagates to the top level, the entire execution is reverted. This differs from an enclosing contract catching and handling an external-call failure.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding atomicity when flash-swap repayment fails

questions.question: A single collateral asset is worth 1,500, its liquidation threshold is 80%, and the debt is worth 1,000. If HF=collateral value×liquidation threshold÷debt value, what is HF?
questions.explanation: HF=1,500×0.8÷1,000=1.2. This calculation assumes the single collateral asset and common value unit specified in the question.
questions.learningObjective: Calculating a health factor

questions.question: Only the collateral price falls in a loan whose debt value and liquidation threshold stay fixed. What happens to the health factor?

options.text: It falls, moving closer to the liquidation threshold
It cannot be calculated unless the debt price changes
It always stays the same because the collateral quantity is unchanged
It rises, automatically eliminating liquidation risk

questions.explanation: The health factor is proportional to collateral value adjusted for the liquidation threshold. Falling collateral value reduces the buffer relative to debt.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding the solvency effect of falling collateral value

questions.question: Part of a positive debt balance is repaid while collateral value and the threshold remain unchanged. How does the health factor change?

options.text: It rises because the denominator decreases
It falls because the denominator decreases
It necessarily becomes 1 regardless of the repayment amount
It does not change because collateral is unchanged

questions.explanation: Other things being equal, less debt means a smaller obligation relative to collateral. Fees and simultaneous price changes are separate factors.
questions.learningObjective: Relating debt repayment to the health factor

questions.question: A price feed shows a number within the normal range, but its last update was a long time ago. What should a lending contract check?

options.text: Use it regardless of update delay if it has enough decimal places
Check the update time and allowed delay to restrict stale values
Use it without checking the update time if it is positive
Assume the value is real-time if the returning function is named latest

questions.explanation: Even a normally formatted number may fail to reflect the current market if it is stale. Freshness checks should match the oracle's update policy.
questions.learningObjective: Checking oracle price freshness

questions.question: A lending contract uses only the instantaneous reserve ratio of a low-liquidity DEX pool to price collateral. What is the central risk?

options.text: A large trade can distort the instantaneous price and induce an incorrect lending valuation
Public reserves mean the ratio cannot be changed by trading
The contract cannot read reserve prices changed in the same block, so it is safe
If the price is restored within one transaction, intermediate lending valuations are unaffected

questions.explanation: Spot prices in small pools are sensitive to trades. Manipulation resistance, such as reliable external observations or suitable time averaging, must be considered.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding manipulation risk in a single pool's spot price

questions.question: Other things being equal, what is an appropriate description of using a longer TWAP observation window?

options.text: It always reduces both manipulability and price-response delay to zero
It uses only the last trade regardless of the time window
It reduces the weight of brief distortions but may respond more slowly to recent changes
It removes past observations and therefore always equals the spot price

questions.explanation: A TWAP averages prices over a period. A longer window reduces the influence of momentary changes but can respond more slowly to a new price.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding the tradeoffs of time-weighted average prices

questions.question: Why does an optimistic rollup's standard withdrawal path include a challenge period?

options.text: To fill a fixed computation interval for re-executing every transaction on L1
To make every channel participant close their channel for each withdrawal
To wait for all users to jointly sign the same withdrawal request
To provide time to challenge an invalid state transition

questions.explanation: Optimistic rollups provide a dispute procedure for submitted results. Fast-withdrawal services may use separate liquidity provision and conditions.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding optimistic-rollup challenge periods

questions.question: In a rollup using validity proofs, what is the central fact the L1 verifier contract seeks to check?

options.text: Whether the external oracle's raw information necessarily corresponds to reality
Whether even unsubmitted transaction data is permanently stored on L1
Whether the new state follows from the previous state under the specified execution rules
Whether every L2 contract is designed to match users' intentions

questions.explanation: A validity proof verifies the correctness of defined computations and state transitions. It does not automatically prove real-world facts or future prices.
questions.learningObjective: Identifying what a validity rollup verifies

questions.question: Which conclusion does the term ZK rollup alone not necessarily support?

options.text: It uses a structure that verifies off-chain execution results
All user transaction details are private
It connects the results of multiple L2 transactions to L1
It verifies execution correctness with validity proofs

questions.explanation: Using ZK-based validity proofs and keeping user data private are separate design choices. ZK rollups can also use public data.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing ZK rollups from transaction confidentiality

questions.question: State-channel participants update and jointly sign their state several times. Which state should be submitted for settlement?

options.text: The latest agreed state with valid joint signatures
Any older state showing the largest amount
The most favorable state written unilaterally by one participant
The earliest state regardless of joint signatures

questions.explanation: State channels determine settlement from signed states and their ordering. Dispute procedures are also designed to respond to submissions of outdated states.
questions.learningObjective: Choosing a state for state-channel closure

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the capacity of a state channel settled using deposited funds?

options.text: A channel counts signatures without verifying amounts
Channel funds can also be freely spent in all external transactions at the same time
The amounts that can be transacted are constrained by deposited funds and their current allocation
Off-chain transactions allow unlimited payments beyond the deposited amount

questions.explanation: Fast channel updates do not mean that unlimited unbacked funds can be created. Channel funds and participant allocations limit what can be settled.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding the constraints of funds locked in a state channel

questions.question: An asset moves from chain A to chain B through a lock-and-mint bridge. What is the basic flow?

options.text: Add the same freely spendable balance on B without locking the asset on A
Register only B's recipient address on A without changing A's balance
Burn the original asset on A and reissue the original only on B
Lock the original on A and mint a corresponding representation on B

questions.explanation: The original is locked in a contract or similar mechanism on the source chain, and a corresponding asset is recorded on the destination chain. Returning it can use the reverse burn-and-release flow.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding asset correspondence in lock-and-mint bridges

questions.question: Why can a bridge lose assets even when both underlying chains operate normally?

options.text: Underlying consensus automatically audits bridge code regardless of which chain hosts it
Healthy underlying chains automatically guarantee that bridge messages are truthful
Locking the original asset makes destination-chain minting-authority checks unnecessary
Bridge contracts and message validators can have separate vulnerabilities

questions.explanation: The connecting layer has its own code and verification assumptions. The safety of the underlying chains alone does not establish bridge safety.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding additional bridge trust assumptions

questions.question: A rollup sequencer returns a success indication immediately after accepting a transaction. What distinction should the user make?

options.text: Paying an L2 fee instantly buys L1 finality
A sequencer signature guarantees redemption of every bridged asset
A sequencer response and L1 validity verification are always the same event
Fast L2 confirmation differs from completed L1 settlement

questions.explanation: A fast acceptance or execution response may not mean that L1 data publication and the proof or dispute procedure are complete. Distinguish the level of finality at each stage.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguishing sequencer confirmation from L1 settlement

questions.question: When comparing two systems using validity proofs, what is the key distinction between a rollup and a validium?

options.text: Whether validity proofs verify state transitions
Where availability of the data needed to reconstruct state is ensured
Whether multiple transactions are processed in batches

questions.explanation: Typically, a ZK rollup provides the necessary data through L1, while a validium uses off-chain data availability. Sharing a proof approach does not make them equivalent.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding data locations in rollups and validiums

questions.question: Why does a rollup batch multiple transactions and submit compressed data to L1?

options.text: To store every transaction's final state only in personal wallets
To spread L1 submission costs across transactions and reduce data volume
To eliminate all signature checks for individual transactions
To make every user store the entire L1 block again

questions.explanation: Batching and compression help lower per-transaction L1 data costs. Lower costs do not mean that transaction-validity checks are omitted.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding transaction batching and shared rollup costs

questions.question: A contract on chain A calls a contract on chain B through a bridge message. What should a typical app design account for?

options.text: The destination chain directly reads the source chain's remaining gas
Successful source processing unconditionally guarantees successful destination execution
Every step on both chains always finishes within the same EVM call stack
Source processing and destination execution may finish at different times

questions.explanation: Cross-chain messaging is an asynchronous flow involving delivery and verification. Apps must manage stage-specific states such as waiting, failure, and retries.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding asynchronous cross-chain calls

questions.question: After bridging a token to another network, an attempt to transfer it reports insufficient gas assets. What should be checked first?

options.text: Only the allowance of the destination token
Only the total supply of the source token contract
The destination network's fee asset and the address's balance of it
Only the balance of the source network's fee asset

questions.explanation: The bridged token may differ from the asset required for fees on the destination chain. Check execution costs and balances separately for each chain.
questions.learningObjective: Preparing execution fees on the destination chain

questions.question: What is the main purpose of including chainId and verifyingContract in an EIP-712 signing domain?

options.text: Reduce the scope for misusing the same message on other chains or contracts
Prevent all reuse of the same message in the same contract without additional state
Allow one signature to be shared across all chains and contracts
Automatically verify the target contract's access-control code

questions.explanation: Domain separation identifies the intended context of a signature, including its chain and contract. The application must handle replay protection within the same domain separately.
questions.learningObjective: Understanding EIP-712 domain separation

questions.question: A wallet displays structured signing data in a readable format. What must be checked before signing?

options.text: Check only the signature hash length and skip the scope of approval
Skip the requesting contract address if the connected wallet address is correct
Whether the approval target, amount, deadline, and verifying contract match the intended action
Assume a gas-free signature cannot affect asset permissions

questions.explanation: Readable formatting helps review but does not make the content itself safe. An off-chain signature can also be submitted as authorization to use assets.
questions.learningObjective: Reviewing structured-signature details

questions.question: You want an EIP-712 message to be usable only once in the same contract. What essential check should be added?

options.text: Record used nonces or message identifiers and reject reuse
Checking chainId is enough even if repeated use in the same contract is allowed
Omit the contract's usage record if the wallet displayed the message once
Repeatedly accept an old nonce as long as the signer address matches
