questions.question: An EIP-2930 access list is an authorization allowlist, so CALLing a contract absent from it makes the transaction invalid for that reason alone even with sufficient gas.
questions.explanation: Access lists are gas-accounting mechanisms that prewarm addresses and slots. Access outside the list remains possible, potentially incurring cold-access costs.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish access lists from authorization allowlists

questions.question: When relative locks apply to a transaction with several inputs, one unsatisfied input lock causes the whole transaction to fail that condition even if every other input is mature.
questions.explanation: All relevant input conditions must be satisfied together. One mature UTXO does not satisfy another input's unmet lock.
questions.learningObjective: Combine relative locks across multiple inputs

questions.question: If two different checkpoints are justified, the older one can always be treated as finalized without checking ancestry, voting links, or epoch spacing.
questions.explanation: Finalization requires particular justification links and epoch relationships. Simply counting two justified checkpoints cannot replace the finalization rules.
questions.learningObjective: Recognize the misconception that two justifications alone imply finality

questions.question: In an EVM with EIP-6780, SELFDESTRUCTing a contract created in an earlier transaction does not remove its code by itself, even if a later transaction attempts CREATE2 deployment of different code at the same address.
questions.explanation: Unless the contract was created in the same transaction, SELFDESTRUCT does not delete code and storage. Redeployment that assumes the existing address's code was erased therefore does not work.
questions.learningObjective: Analyze how retaining old contract code affects CREATE2 redeployment

questions.question: Combining partial signatures in PSBTs requires checking that they concern the same unsigned transaction; signatures from two transactions with different outputs must not be mixed as approvals of one transaction.
questions.explanation: PSBT combines multiple participants' work on the same transaction. Different underlying transactions must not be treated as the same signing target.
questions.learningObjective: Understand the same-transaction prerequisite for collaborative signing

questions.question: With 7 equally weighted nodes and at most 2 Byzantine nodes, requiring signatures from only 4 distinct nodes guarantees that any two certificates share an honest signer.
questions.explanation: Two sets of 4 may intersect in only 1 node, which can be Byzantine. A simple majority alone does not guarantee an honest intersection.
questions.learningObjective: Understand the limits of simple-majority quorums

questions.question: If external function signatures remain unchanged across an upgrade, internal function pointers stored in storage always safely point to the same functions in the new implementation.
questions.explanation: Implementation changes can alter internal function code locations. An unchanged external ABI alone does not guarantee continued validity of internal function pointers.
questions.learningObjective: Understand code upgrades and function locations

questions.question: Even in a PoS configuration with different effective stakes per validator, the 2/3 finalization threshold can always be determined by counting signing validators alone.
questions.explanation: In stake-weighted consensus, headcount and voting weight can differ. Calculate the threshold using the effective weights and total denominator in the relevant state.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish validator count from stake weight

questions.question: If an ERC-4337 paymaster has enough locked stake, that stake automatically acts as the same balance when its EntryPoint fee deposit is insufficient, making deposit checks unnecessary.
questions.explanation: Stake and deposit serve different purposes. A sufficient deposit is needed to pay gas costs; locked stake alone does not replace this check.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish paymaster stake from its fee deposit

questions.question: If EIP-7702 delegated account A points to B and B points to C, the EVM must follow delegation recursively until it reaches an account without a delegation designator and execute C's code.
questions.explanation: Resolving delegated code follows only the first delegation. If the target also contains a delegation designator, resolution does not continue to its target.
questions.learningObjective: Understand code-resolution limits for chained delegation designators

questions.question: In an EIP-7702 transaction that passes global format validation, an authorization tuple whose signed nonce differs from its authority account's nonce is skipped, and the next tuple is checked.
questions.explanation: A nonce mismatch during tuple validation stops processing that tuple and moves to the next. Distinguish this from a formatting error in the transaction itself.
questions.learningObjective: Determine the scope of authorization-tuple validation failure

questions.question: In an ERC-4626 vault with withdrawal fees, convertToAssets always equals exactly the net assets received by actually redeeming the same shares.
questions.explanation: Conversion functions represent idealized conversions and differ from queries reflecting actual conditions such as fees. To estimate receipts, use the appropriate function, such as previewRedeem, and check execution conditions.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish conversions from actual withdrawal estimates

questions.question: The EIP-6780 deletion exception applies whenever creation and destruction occur in the same block, so a contract created in a block's first transaction and SELFDESTRUCTed in its second also loses its code.
questions.explanation: The exception requires the same transaction, not merely the same block. Separate transactions do not qualify even when included in one block.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish same-block from same-transaction conditions

questions.question: An SSZ container has a uint16 field a followed by a variable-length byte list b, whose offset field is 4 bytes. With no other fields, b's data begins 6 bytes from the container's start.
questions.explanation: The fixed section contains 2 bytes for a and a 4-byte offset to b. Variable data therefore begins at 2+4=6 bytes.
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the start offset of fixed and variable sections

questions.question: Under EIP-2929, warming slot 5 in contract A does not by itself warm slot 5 in contract B.
questions.explanation: A storage access-set entry is a pair of contract address and storage key. Equal slot numbers at different addresses are different access targets.
questions.learningObjective: Apply address-and-slot pairs as storage-access keys

questions.question: After EIP-6780, a contract created in an earlier transaction that SELFDESTRUCTs with itself as beneficiary must burn its existing ETH balance and leave it at zero.
questions.explanation: In this case the contract is not deleted, and transferring its balance to itself leaves its net balance unchanged. Distinguish this from the exception for contracts created in the same transaction.
questions.learningObjective: Determine the result of an existing contract sending its balance to itself

questions.question: In Fabric, T1 and T2 both simulate after reading K at version v1. If valid T1 updates K earlier in the same block, later T2 can fail MVCC validation of its v1 read.
questions.explanation: Validation incorporates updates from earlier valid transactions in the same block as well as previous blocks. The version T2 read then differs from the version at validation.
questions.learningObjective: Trace the effect of earlier valid writes in the same block on read versions

questions.question: If two paths in an SSZ multiproof share an auxiliary node, the identical hash must still be transmitted separately for each path to permit verification.
questions.explanation: Multiproofs can supply shared auxiliary nodes once and reuse them. This can reduce proof size compared with simply concatenating all individual proofs.
questions.learningObjective: Understand deduplication of proof nodes shared by multiple paths

questions.question: A valid balance proof against a trusted past block's state root does not establish the same current balance unless subsequent state changes have been verified.
questions.explanation: A state proof guarantees a particular root and time. Current balances or spendability require the necessary current state and evidence.
questions.learningObjective: Understand the scope of a correct historical state proof

questions.question: Even if an ERC-4626 vault pauses deposits so maxDeposit returns 0, previewDeposit in the same state can return a positive share conversion that ignores the deposit limit.
questions.explanation: Preview functions estimate conversion results without restricting them by deposit limits. Actual permitted amounts are determined separately through max functions and execution conditions.
questions.learningObjective: Understand the independence of preview values and deposit limits

questions.question: EIP-1153 TSTORE applies the same gas-stipend check as SSTORE, so it must fail when remaining gas is 2,300 or less even if its own operation cost is covered.
questions.explanation: TSTORE does not apply that SSTORE stipend check. Outside a static context, it can execute with 2,300 gas or less if enough gas remains for the operation.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish SSTORE's gas-stipend restriction from TSTORE

questions.question: Verifying codeHash under a trusted stateRoot using an EIP-1186 account proof does not by itself mean the contract's complete bytecode has been provided.
questions.explanation: The account proof verifies account fields including codeHash. Code can be obtained separately and hashed for comparison with that verified codeHash.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish an account proof's codeHash from provision of actual code

questions.question: SSZ serialization includes all field names and type information within its bytes, so a recipient can always deserialize it uniquely without knowing the schema beforehand.
questions.explanation: SSZ is not self-describing. Correct interpretation requires knowing the expected types and structure.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish serialized data from its external schema

questions.question: Once a source-chain deposit is sufficiently finalized, separate risks from unlimited implementation-upgrade authority held by the destination bridge's administrator are eliminated.
questions.explanation: Source-chain finality guarantees the source deposit history. Upgrades, key management, and accounting defects in the destination contract remain separate trust assumptions and attack surfaces.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish source finality from upgrade risk

questions.question: PBFT's limit of f faults applies equally to malicious clients and replicas, so more than f malicious clients automatically removes safety guarantees even if every replica is honest.
questions.explanation: That PBFT fault bound concerns replicas. Client-request authorization and state invariants require separate validation, but malicious-client count is not constrained by the same f.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish client faults from replica faults

questions.question: Validators on physically separate servers can still suffer correlated failures from the same defective client implementation, even when hardware failures have been isolated.
questions.explanation: Independent servers and independent software-failure domains are different concepts. Identical malfunction across many validators can simultaneously affect consensus fault bounds and slashing risk.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish separate servers from client diversity

questions.question: Under EIP-1153, after A executes TSTORE(0,7) and calls B through an ordinary CALL, B must read 7 with TLOAD(0) even if B has never written that slot.
questions.explanation: An ordinary CALL uses target B's transient storage. Equal slot numbers do not share A's storage; a slot B has not written in this transaction contains 0.
questions.learningObjective: Identify contract-specific transient-storage isolation in ordinary CALLs

questions.question: If EIP-7702 authorization processing successfully updates delegation code and the authority account nonce, a later execution revert does not undo those already processed delegation changes or nonce increments.
questions.explanation: The authorization list is processed before execution. Failure of the later execution stage preserves the earlier delegation-designator updates and authority-account nonce increases.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish rollback scope for authorization processing and execution failure

questions.question: EIP-2930 permits listing the same address twice in an access list without storage keys. At 2,400 gas per address entry, those entries cost 4,800 gas.
questions.explanation: Duplicate addresses are permitted but each entry is charged. In the warm-address set used during execution, repeating an address provides no separate benefit.
questions.learningObjective: Calculate validity and charges for duplicate access-list entries

questions.question: An EIP-2930 transaction pays the upfront gas cost for listed addresses or storage keys even if execution never uses them.
questions.explanation: List costs are calculated from entry counts before execution. An unused entry is not exempt from that upfront cost.
questions.learningObjective: Determine costs for unused access-list entries

questions.question: Under EIP-6780, an ETH balance existing at an address before contract creation does not by itself remove the deletion exception when the contract is created and SELFDESTRUCTed in that same transaction.
questions.explanation: A preexisting ETH balance does not change whether the contract was created in the current transaction. Creation and SELFDESTRUCT within one transaction retain the earlier deletion behavior.
questions.learningObjective: Relate preexisting balances to the same-transaction deletion exception

questions.question: Two ERC-4337 UserOperations using the same account and key can both be validly processed in one successful bundle with the same sequence as long as their signatures differ.
questions.explanation: Different signatures do not bypass sequence validation for the same account and key. An operation reusing the sequence consumed by the first fails nonce validation.
questions.learningObjective: Identify duplicate UserOperations in the same nonce channel

questions.question: In Fabric, two transactions meeting every other validation condition can both be valid if they write different values to K without reading K, leaving the later transaction's value.
questions.explanation: MVCC checks version dependencies in the read set. Two writes with no read dependency on K do not necessarily make one invalid solely because both write the same key.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish validation outcomes for writes without read dependencies

questions.question: For ERC-1271 contract verification, low-level call success and return of the standard success magic value are separate conditions; absence of a revert alone must not be treated as signature approval.
questions.explanation: A contract function can return successfully while returning a value that indicates an invalid signature. Check the approval return value defined by the standard.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish successful calls from signature approval

questions.question: A Bitcoin block timestamp can be lower than its immediate predecessor's while meeting applicable consensus conditions such as past median time, so it must not be interpreted as a strictly increasing wall-clock record.
questions.explanation: Timestamps are constrained by factors such as the median of earlier blocks, rather than a simple requirement to exceed the immediately preceding block. They do not directly prove precise real-world transaction times either.
questions.learningObjective: Understand non-monotonic block timestamps

questions.question: Even if multiplying Pedersen commitments under the same group and generators produces a commitment to the message sum, that alone does not prove each message lies in the application's permitted amount range.
questions.explanation: Homomorphic operations preserve addition modulo the group order. Proving nonnegativity or individual upper bounds requires separate proofs constraining those ranges.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish commitment addition from amount ranges

questions.question: Including an Ethereum validator's voluntary-exit message immediately eliminates all possibility of slashing for its past conflicting signatures.
questions.explanation: An exit request, the end of active participation, and withdrawability are different events. Past conflicting behavior can still be slashable under the applicable conditions, including before the specified withdrawable time.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish exit messages from the slashability period

questions.question: In a conventional storage layout, two uint128 values can share one 32-byte slot, and updating one can require reading, modifying, and writing to preserve the other's bits.
questions.explanation: Packing small values can reduce storage slots but does not always reduce gas for every access. Preserving other bits in the same slot can require extra work.
questions.learningObjective: Update individual values sharing one storage slot

questions.question: A proof being noninteractive is enough to conclude that every such system necessarily requires a trusted setup ceremony involving destruction of secrets.
questions.explanation: Noninteractivity and setup trust assumptions are different classification dimensions. Noninteractive proof systems can also operate with transparent public parameters.
questions.learningObjective: Understand the relationship between noninteractive proofs and trusted setup

questions.question: A PoS node returning after a long offline period does not obtain sufficient independent trust merely by receiving the same checkpoint from several servers controlled by one operator.
questions.explanation: Weak-subjectivity checkpoints require recency and trustworthy confirmation paths. Multiple responses from one administrative domain should not be counted as independent evidence.
questions.learningObjective: Avoid treating replicas of one source as independent evidence

questions.question: When SSZ binary-merkleizes three 32-byte chunks, the Merkle root is always obtained by concatenating them and hashing once, without padding or intermediate nodes.
questions.explanation: SSZ organizes chunks into a binary tree with necessary padding and staged hash calculations. This differs from hashing a simple concatenation of three chunks once.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish binary merkleization of 32-byte chunks from hashing concatenated data

questions.question: Summing every historical vote from a validator when calculating LMD-GHOST weight departs from its latest-message-based approach.
questions.explanation: LMD means latest message driven and uses each validator's latest relevant vote. The same stake does not gain duplicate weight merely by having sent many older messages.
questions.learningObjective: Calculate weights based on latest messages

questions.question: In OpenZeppelin's approach, disabling an implementation's initializer in its constructor does not block legitimate initialization in an uninitialized proxy context through the same storage flag, because the proxy has separate storage.
questions.explanation: The implementation and proxy maintain initialization state in separate storage. Distinguish preventing direct initialization attacks on the implementation from properly initializing a new proxy.
questions.learningObjective: Separate initialization state of implementations and proxies

questions.question: Signing an EIP-7702 authorization with chain_id=0 binds it exclusively to the single chain used when signing.
questions.explanation: chain_id=0 does not bind authorization to one specific chain ID. It can be valid on other chains when the remaining conditions, such as nonce and account state, hold.
questions.learningObjective: Understand the scope of delegation signatures with chain ID zero

questions.question: An EIP-1186 storage proof can be verified through a valid trie path showing that a key's leaf is absent, and this can establish the storage slot's default value of 0.
questions.explanation: An absence proof uses features such as an empty position or a different key's leaf on the search path. Apply verified absence together with the storage default-value rule.
questions.learningObjective: Understand trie absence proofs

questions.question: On a chain implementing EIP-7702, an EOA with a valid delegation designator cannot originate an ordinary transaction under any circumstances because its code is nonempty.
questions.explanation: EIP-7702 makes an exception allowing EOAs with valid delegation designators to keep sending transactions. Other validity conditions, including nonce, signature, and balance, still apply.
questions.learningObjective: Understand the delegated-account exception to restrictions on senders with code

questions.question: Sending a swap through a private relay instead of the public mempool removes the need to consider later state changes or order processors, so removing the on-chain minimum-received check provides identical protection.
questions.explanation: Reducing public exposure does not remove every ordering, state, or trust risk. The lower bound on actual execution results must be checked separately on-chain.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish private order delivery from protection of execution conditions

questions.question: In a general Merkle tree that commits to no sorting or key-position rules, an inclusion proof for A also proves B's absence merely because B is not visible in that proof.
questions.explanation: An inclusion path does not reveal the complete contents of other branches. Non-inclusion proofs need additional structure, such as ordering or a key space, and evidence appropriate to that structure.
questions.learningObjective: Avoid inferring absence from inclusion of another leaf

questions.question: Even when BFT consensus guarantees the same execution order at every honest replica, consensus alone does not prevent an authorized user from submitting business data that is factually or operationally wrong.
questions.explanation: Consensus safety guarantees consistent execution. Applications must separately define and validate factual accuracy, business rules, and permission scope.
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish consistent execution from input meaning

questions.question: An EIP-2930 transaction's access list is excluded from the sender's signed content, so a relayer can arbitrarily edit the list without obtaining a new signature while preserving signature validity.
questions.explanation: The signing hash includes the transaction type and payload, including the access list. Editing the list changes the transaction content authorized by the original signature.
questions.learningObjective: Understand how signatures restrict access-list changes

questions.question: Even with sufficient total Lightning channel capacity, a route may be unable to carry the requested payment if its available balance in the payment direction is insufficient.
questions.explanation: Channel capacity and directional balances are different quantities. Route bottlenecks, fees, reserves, and HTLC constraints also matter.
questions.learningObjective: Assess statements about channel directionality and explain why

questions.question: Even without overflow, integer expressions (a/b)×c and (a×c)/b are always equal for all integers a, b, and c.
questions.explanation: Intermediate division can truncate fractional parts. For a=7, b=10, and c=3, the first gives 0 and the second 2, so units and rounding direction must be considered.
questions.learningObjective: Assess statements about operation order and explain why

questions.question: Even if an administrator cannot withdraw directly, their ability to grant new roles or approve arbitrary spenders requires examining whether they can indirectly obtain asset-transfer authority.
questions.explanation: Access control cannot be assessed from one function's modifier alone. Connect the authorization paths involving role management, approvals, upgrades, and external calls.
questions.learningObjective: Assess statements about authorization graphs and explain why

questions.question: If an RPC connection fails after transaction submission, the transaction definitely reached no node, so resending with a new nonce has no duplication risk.
questions.explanation: Submission may have succeeded while only the response was lost. Check the existing hash and nonce, chain state, and business-request records before deciding to retry.
questions.learningObjective: Assess interpretations of RPC errors and explain why

questions.question: Voting snapshots and timelocks make long-term accumulation by large holders, vote buying, execution-authority bypasses, and similar threats mathematically impossible.
questions.explanation: Snapshots and delays restrict particular attack paths without removing every economic or operational risk. Assess permission structure, participation, concentration, and bypass paths together.
questions.learningObjective: Assess claims of absolute governance safety and explain why

questions.question: Removing mint authority necessarily eliminates the ability to freeze token accounts even if freeze authority remains.
questions.explanation: Additional issuance and freezing have separate authority fields and roles. Removing one does not automatically remove the other.
questions.learningObjective: Assess statements about separate freeze authority and explain why

questions.question: In a fee-free lock-and-mint bridge, burning 50 representation tokens and releasing 50 locked underlying tokens can preserve the correspondence between the remaining amounts.
questions.explanation: A normal withdrawal pairs the decrease in representation assets with the decrease in held assets. This conservation relationship assumes no duplicate messages or invalid burn proofs.
questions.learningObjective: Assess conservation in valid withdrawals and explain why

questions.question: If profit or loss on BTC-settled futures is the same 0.1 BTC, its dollar value is always identical even when the closing BTC price differs.
questions.explanation: Dollar profit or loss equals BTC profit or loss multiplied by the conversion price, so it varies with price. Distinguish settlement-currency results from reporting-currency results.
questions.learningObjective: Assess inverse-contract conversions and explain why

questions.question: Even if a commitment cannot be changed, a final revealer who can withhold their value after seeing others' values can still affect outcome selection or halt progress.
questions.explanation: Commitment binding and progress through revelation are different guarantees. Design penalties for non-revelation, deadlines, recovery rules, and related measures.
questions.learningObjective: Assess statements about aborting reveals and explain why

questions.question: Buying a token redeemable for 1 underlying unit at 0.95 units guarantees a net profit of 0.05 units even with redemption delays, contract losses, and transfer costs.
questions.explanation: Account for redemption conditions, risks during the wait, and every cost. The quoted discount is a price difference needing analysis, not guaranteed net income.
questions.learningObjective: Assess redemption-arbitrage claims and explain why

questions.question: Querying collateral, debt, and prices against the same block hash can reduce problems from mixing values across different blocks.
questions.explanation: Values from different times can combine into a state that never existed. Queries from one snapshot and checks of canonical-chain membership support consistent analysis.
questions.learningObjective: Assess statements about same-block queries and explain why

questions.question: When an NFT receiving callback can make additional transfers, there are situations where final ownerOf must be checked separately even after the initial transfer succeeds.
questions.explanation: Callbacks can cause further state changes, so the initial destination may differ from the final owner. Validate required business invariants against the state at call completion.
questions.learningObjective: Assess ownership after hooks and explain why

questions.question: Making an initializer callable only once removes administrator-takeover risk without checking who makes the first call.
questions.explanation: Limiting execution count does not establish the first caller's eligibility. Safely link initialization with deployment or upgrades and validate caller authorization.
questions.learningObjective: Assess initialization protections and explain why

questions.question: If an implementation allows transfer of a vesting vault's beneficiary position through ownership transfer, that claim position may be transferred even while the tokens remain locked.
questions.explanation: A restriction on immediate token withdrawal can differ from transfer of vault ownership holding future claims. Check the actual vesting implementation's ownership-transfer functions and rights structure.
questions.learningObjective: Assess statements about vesting ownership and explain why

questions.question: Moving Lightning channel liquidity through a circular payment always increases total assets by more than its fees without any external funding.
questions.explanation: Rebalancing changes the location and direction of funds without creating value. Routing fees can instead reduce net assets.
questions.learningObjective: Assess statements about circular rebalancing and explain why

questions.question: Accepting a new validator set requires an important verification link establishing that the transition was legitimately authorized from the existing trusted state.
questions.explanation: An arbitrary set's ability to produce valid signatures does not make it the chain's legitimate successor set. Preserve authentication across client-state transitions.
questions.learningObjective: Assess validator-set transitions and explain why

questions.question: If price is stored with an 8-decimal scale and quantity with an 18-decimal scale, their product still has only an 18-decimal scale.
questions.explanation: The product scale is 10^8×10^18=10^26. Apply correct division and rounding for the intended display unit.
questions.learningObjective: Assess fixed-point-price calculations and explain why

questions.question: If 4 honest values among 7 feeds all lie within 90–110, the median remains in that range even when the other 3 values are arbitrary.
questions.explanation: For the sorted fourth value to lie outside the honest majority's range, at least four values would need to lie outside it. This relies on the feed count, honest-majority, and simultaneous-observation assumptions.
questions.learningObjective: Assess median bounds and explain why

questions.question: Recovering a Bitcoin multisig wallet may require the public-key configuration, key order, and derivation paths of existing outputs as well as enough signing seeds.
questions.explanation: Being able to sign differs from reconstructing an existing spending script exactly. Backing up policy information such as descriptors can improve recoverability.
questions.learningObjective: Assess recovery-policy information and explain why

questions.question: Adding nonReentrant to a contract's withdraw function eliminates every risk from external protocols using that contract's temporarily inconsistent view results.
questions.explanation: A lock on one function does not automatically protect other functions or what external contracts observe and do. Review shared state and assumptions about read paths together.
questions.learningObjective: Assess reentrancy-lock scope and explain why

questions.topic: Voting power at a specified time
questions.question: Fixing voting power at a past checkpoint can reduce the problem of tokens borrowed briefly during a voting transaction immediately counting as that historical voting power.
questions.explanation: Fixed historical voting power differs from using current balances directly. It does not solve every issue involving borrowing before the snapshot or long-term control.
questions.learningObjective: Assess time-specific voting power and explain why

questions.question: When aggregating same-symbol representation assets issued by several bridges against one reserve, differences in collateral claims across their issuance routes may be ignored.
questions.explanation: Each bridge may have separate collateral, verification, and redemption structures. A shared name does not prove interchangeability or identical claims.
questions.learningObjective: Assess bridge-route equivalence and explain why

questions.question: When a liquidator repays part of a debt and takes collateral with a bonus, the remaining HF necessarily exceeds 1 for every initial collateral-to-debt ratio.
questions.explanation: Repayment reduces debt, but the bonus can remove more collateral. Depending on the initial state, liquidation size, bonus, and threshold, the account may remain liquidatable.
questions.learningObjective: Assess combined liquidation effects and explain why

questions.question: Matching price changes on 10 spot units and a short position of 10 linear futures units can offset price profit and loss, while withdrawal failure at one exchange remains a risk.
questions.explanation: Offsetting price risk does not remove counterparty or custody risk. Manage access to assets and margin requirements at each exchange separately.
questions.learningObjective: Assess notional hedges and explain why

questions.question: Solidity negative integer division truncates toward zero, so it can differ from average-tick calculations requiring mathematical floor rounding.
questions.explanation: For example, −7/3 yields −2, while the floor is −3. Check the required adjustment when the value is negative and has a remainder.
questions.learningObjective: Assess negative-average calculations and explain why

questions.question: In a multichain app, an address-only balance cache that omits chain ID and token contract is always correct whenever the address strings match.
questions.explanation: The same address can have different assets and states across chains. Include network, asset, and the necessary query time in cache keys.
questions.learningObjective: Assess cache keys and explain why

questions.question: An arbitrary relayer's signature over a remote-chain block, made with its own private key, proves that remote chain's consensus finality by itself.
questions.explanation: A carrier's signature differs from the remote chain's consensus proof. The receiving chain must validate headers and proofs under the relevant light-client and consensus rules.
questions.learningObjective: Assess relayer-signature claims and explain why

questions.question: Even with recoverable assets exceeding liabilities, delayed asset sales or redemptions may prevent meeting same-day withdrawal demands.
questions.explanation: Economic solvency and cash liquidity over time require separate assessment. Maturity mismatches or fire-sale discounts can increase risk during concentrated redemptions.
questions.learningObjective: Assess liquidity and solvency and explain why

questions.question: A valid VRF proof automatically guarantees a legitimate application outcome regardless of which round receives it, even without checking the response requestId.
questions.explanation: Correct randomness generation and association with an application request are separate conditions. Verify per-request state and IDs to avoid using another round's response.
questions.learningObjective: Assess association of verified randomness and explain why

questions.question: A high total asset value deposited across a Uniswap v3 pool necessarily means proportionately high active liquidity near the current price.
questions.explanation: Deposits can be concentrated in ranges far from current prices. Actual order price impact depends on active liquidity and tick distribution along the execution path.
questions.learningObjective: Assess statements about active liquidity and explain why

questions.question: In a Poisson model, standard deviation divided by mean rises proportionally with the mean block count, so larger pools necessarily have greater relative variability.
questions.explanation: Poisson standard deviation is the square root of the mean, making relative variability 1/√λ. Higher expected block counts reduce relative variability in this simple model.
questions.learningObjective: Assess mining-variance statements and explain why

questions.question: Even if an 18-decimal token's raw balance exceeds JavaScript Number's safe integer range, converting it back to a string restores any lost precision.
questions.explanation: String conversion cannot recover integer information already lost during floating-point conversion. Preserve exact representations such as BigInt or integer strings from the outset.
questions.learningObjective: Assess JavaScript amount handling and explain why

questions.question: An indexer handling reorganizations can maintain consistent accounting more easily if it can reverse deposits applied from blocks removed from the canonical chain.
questions.explanation: Processing new events may need to be accompanied by reversing earlier block changes. Block-hash-based records and reprocessing procedures are important.
questions.learningObjective: Assess canonical-chain accounting and explain why

questions.question: An IPFS CID stored on-chain guarantees that its content can be downloaded at every future time even if nobody retains the file.
questions.explanation: A content address identifies bytes but does not automatically guarantee storage nodes or delivery. Availability requires measures such as pinning, replication, and long-term retention policies.
questions.learningObjective: Assess data-retention claims and explain why

questions.question: If a user-supplied Solana account's data bytes match the expected format, using it as trusted state without checking its owner program is always safe.
questions.explanation: An arbitrary account can supply data with the same format. Verify its actual controlling program, expected address, and relationships to other accounts.
questions.learningObjective: Assess account-owner checks and explain why

questions.question: When integrating Token-2022 tokens, extensions such as transfer fees and hooks can affect assumptions based on simple transfers.
questions.explanation: Beyond program-ID support, review how extensions affect amounts, permissions, and external calls. Explicitly restricting unsupported behaviors may also be necessary.
questions.learningObjective: Assess token extensions and explain why

questions.question: For bridge deposits of fee-on-transfer tokens, minting the requested amount always preserves backing even when the requested quantity differs from the amount actually locked.
questions.explanation: Minting more than actually received can make representation-token claims exceed held assets. Verify the link between actual receipts, locked assets, and issued amounts.
questions.learningObjective: Assess locked-amount accounting and explain why

questions.question: If a light client's trusting period expires, correctly formatted proof data alone must not unconditionally extend the previous trust.
questions.explanation: Client validation includes assumptions about time and validator-set changes. Updates and recovery after expiration must also follow the protocol's validation rules.
questions.learningObjective: Assess IBC trusting periods and explain why

questions.question: When executing a CPI with strong vault authority, restricting the target program ID and the permissions passed through accounts is important.
questions.explanation: Passing trusted vault authority while calling an arbitrary program can permit unexpected actions. Validate the target, instruction, and account relationships together.
questions.learningObjective: Assess CPI trust boundaries and explain why

questions.question: Even with multiple hops on a Lightning route, adding a single base fee to the final received amount always calculates total routing costs exactly.
questions.explanation: Each hop's base fee, proportional fee, and forwarded amount must be included. Fees at later hops can affect earlier forwarded amounts, potentially requiring backward calculation.
questions.learningObjective: Assess route-fee calculations and explain why

questions.question: Showing both control of reserve wallets and inclusion of customer liabilities does not automatically prove the absence of undisclosed external security interests.
questions.explanation: Each proof guarantees only its defined data and statement. Other asset claims and omitted liabilities may require additional information and verification.
questions.learningObjective: Assess reserve-asset evidence and explain why

questions.question: Consistently deriving a nullifier from the same secret credential and usage domain, then checking usage history, can restrict repeated use.
questions.explanation: The circuit must bind the value so users cannot freely choose a new one each time. Design domain separation to fit privacy and the intended usage scope.
questions.learningObjective: Assess zero-knowledge nullifiers and explain why

questions.question: A position borrowing an underlying asset against LST collateral can retain LST depegging risk relative to that asset even if external fiat-price exposure is offset.
questions.explanation: Collateral and debt can change relative price despite appearing to share underlying exposure. Redemption delays, liquidity, and slashing can alter relative value and affect account health.
questions.learningObjective: Assess risk propagation and explain why

questions.question: Even if a ZK proof's public inputs omit the actual payout asset, valid proof bytes guarantee the same statement regardless of which token is paid.
questions.explanation: Without binding the proof to the execution asset, it may be reused with a different meaning. Bind important execution parameters, including asset and domain as well as recipient and amount, into the statement.
questions.learningObjective: Assess commitment sufficiency and explain why

questions.question: Three price feeds at different addresses automatically have independent errors even if all replicate the same external source.
questions.explanation: Separate addresses and independent data sources are different things. A wrong common source can cause multiple feeds to report the same error simultaneously.
questions.learningObjective: Assess multiple-feed assumptions and explain why

questions.question: If a white paper states a daily withdrawal limit but the contract checks only per-transaction limits, splitting withdrawals across transactions still automatically enforces the daily limit.
questions.explanation: Without tracking cumulative spending over the period, repeated-transaction totals may not be limited. Verify that the policy exists in actual state and checking logic.
questions.learningObjective: Assess documented limits and explain why

questions.question: Giving an xpub to an external query service does not increase its ability to link and analyze multiple addresses along that path.
questions.explanation: An xpub can derive public addresses. It does not grant signing authority but can affect privacy through address linking.
questions.learningObjective: Assess extended-public-key exposure and explain why

questions.question: Upgrading to safe code after an incident automatically deletes every allowance and administrator role previously acquired by an attacker.
questions.explanation: Upgrades typically change code while preserving stored state. Existing approvals, permissions, and altered accounting must be checked and recovered separately.
questions.learningObjective: Assess state recovery and explain why

questions.question: Using the same program ID and fixed seed to derive a PDA automatically creates a different vault address for every user.
questions.explanation: Identical derivation inputs produce the same address. User-specific separation requires including a user or vault identifier in the seeds and separately verifying access rights.
questions.learningObjective: Assess PDA separation and explain why

questions.question: When a receipt from a lending protocol is deposited into another vault, the sum of their TVLs always equals net inflows of new external funds.
questions.explanation: The same underlying assets can be counted across multiple layers. Summed TVL is not the same measure as net inflows or deduplicated total assets.
questions.learningObjective: Assess aggregated TVL and explain why

questions.question: With collateral valuation and the threshold fixed, reducing only debt using external funds increases HF while debt remains positive.
questions.explanation: A fixed numerator divided by a smaller positive denominator produces a larger HF. Simultaneous collateral withdrawals or changes in interest or prices require separate analysis.
questions.learningObjective: Assess repayment with external funds and explain why

questions.question: For prices 4 and 9 over equal periods, the arithmetic mean is 6.5 and the geometric mean is 6, so the two methods can differ even with identical inputs.
questions.explanation: The arithmetic mean is 13/2 and the geometric mean is √36. An oracle's economic meaning depends on its averaging method and cumulative variables.
questions.learningObjective: Assess averaging methods and explain why

questions.question: In a stationary Poisson block-arrival model with a 10-minute mean interval, the probability of no block in 10 minutes is e^−1, which is not zero.
questions.explanation: The expected block count is 1, so P(N=0)=e^−1≈36.8%. The mean interval is the average of a probability distribution, not a fixed deadline.
questions.learningObjective: Assess mining probabilities and explain why

questions.question: Splitting a large constant-product-pool order into consecutive parts necessarily restores final reserves to their original values even without other trades or fees.
questions.explanation: Same-direction split trades change reserves cumulatively. Splitting alone does not eliminate price impact or create new assets.
questions.learningObjective: Assess sequential AMM prices and explain why

questions.question: If a price is positive and its decimals are correct, a stale updatedAt or the period immediately after L2 sequencer recovery cannot affect lending safety.
questions.explanation: Positive-value and unit checks do not resolve stale data or unequal access after outages. Review freshness, sequencer status, and recovery grace-period policies separately.
questions.learningObjective: Assess price-check sufficiency and explain why

questions.question: Even if a concentrated-liquidity position stays out of range for a long time, it always receives its overall share of every trading fee in the pool.
questions.explanation: Concentrated-liquidity fees are distributed according to liquidity actively contributing at that time. Do not confuse this with simple proportional distribution over all deposited assets.
questions.learningObjective: Assess out-of-range earnings and explain why

questions.question: Because an external view call does not directly write state, an incorrect return value poses no risk to the caller's state-changing decisions.
questions.explanation: Callers can use return values to decide prices, limits, or eligibility. The trustworthiness, timing, and error handling of external reads remain security concerns.
questions.learningObjective: Assess read-only safety and explain why

questions.question: Even if a service's own contract is immutable, changes to an upgradeable token it uses can affect the service.
questions.explanation: Integrated services rely on the behavior of external assets and programs. Include dependency upgrade, minting, and freezing authority in the trust model.
questions.learningObjective: Assess dependency immutability and explain why

questions.question: Administrative authority to upgrade verification keys or circuits can change what statement is proved and should therefore fall within audit scope.
questions.explanation: Cryptographic verification assumes the meaning of a specific circuit and key. Upgrade procedures, permissions, delays, and validation of new specifications matter.
questions.learningObjective: Assess changes to proved statements and explain why

questions.question: Treating logs from every contract as deposits of an official token merely because their event name is Transfer creates a risk of crediting forged assets.
questions.explanation: Other contracts can use the same event name. Validate chain, official contract, event format, recipient, and canonical-chain status.
questions.learningObjective: Assess log provenance and explain why

questions.question: Passing an administrator's public address in an account list and including the administrator's valid signature in the transaction are separate conditions to verify.
questions.explanation: Anyone can reference a known address. Authorized operations must check address matching, required signer flags, and relevant relationships together.
questions.learningObjective: Assess Solana account authorization and explain why

questions.question: Constraining only b×q=a uniquely fixes q to zero when a=b=0, making a nonzero-denominator check unnecessary.
questions.explanation: 0×q=0 holds for every q. Verifying the intended division statement requires adding missing constraints such as a nonzero denominator.
questions.learningObjective: Assess circuit denominators and explain why

questions.question: Solana loan repayment must check that a token account's mint matches the debt token as well as checking balance amount and holder.
questions.explanation: Equal quantities of assets from different mints are not the same debt repayment. Validate asset identity together with the token program and account permissions.
questions.learningObjective: Assess token identity and explain why

questions.question: Checking that execution matches the target, amount, and calldata approved by a vote can reduce the risk of substituting different execution under an unchanged description.
questions.explanation: Bind human-readable proposal descriptions to actual execution bytes. Proposal identifiers and execution checks must commit precisely to the approved effects.
questions.learningObjective: Assess proposal-to-execution binding and explain why

questions.question: If an annualized reward rate exceeds the borrowing rate, realized profit is always positive regardless of collateral revaluation, funding fees, or reinvestment fees.
questions.explanation: Prices, quantities, costs, and payout conditions matter in addition to those two rates. Assess net profit or loss by combining all cash flows over matching units and periods.
questions.learningObjective: Assess cumulative costs and explain why

questions.question: In a fee-free constant-product pool with X=200 and Y=300, receiving 100 Y requires an input of 100 X.
questions.explanation: The product is 60,000. After the trade Y=200, requiring X=300. The difference from the original 200 is an input of 100, unlike a conversion assuming constant price.
questions.learningObjective: Assess AMM exact-output calculations and explain why

questions.question: Consolidating multiple UTXOs when fees are low never reveals additional links between addresses, regardless of potential future fee savings.
questions.explanation: Using several inputs together can reveal more evidence of common control. Fee savings and privacy effects should be considered separately.
questions.learningObjective: Assess UTXO consolidation and explain why

questions.question: An on-chain linear token-vesting schedule makes transfers of economic rights through vault ownership or off-exchange contracts impossible in every case.
questions.explanation: A restricted withdrawal schedule can coexist with transfer of vault ownership or separate rights. Distinguish the lock's technical scope from the economic transferability of claims.
questions.learningObjective: Assess locks and transfers of rights and explain why

questions.question: If a state-changing function updates only part of its accounting before an external call, another contract can read intermediate state through a view function and use an incorrect price.
questions.explanation: Read calls can affect other systems' behavior. Review invariants at externally observable points and consistency of shared state.
questions.learningObjective: Assess observation of intermediate state and explain why

questions.question: In a Poisson process with constant hash rate and difficulty, after 20 minutes without a block, the expected additional wait for the next block remains the original mean.
questions.explanation: Exponential interarrival times in a Poisson process are memoryless. If actual network hash rate or difficulty changes, the stationary-model assumption must be reconsidered.
questions.learningObjective: Assess Poisson waiting times and explain why

questions.question: Even if a CPI changes an account balance, every framework necessarily updates a balance cached before the call to the current value automatically.
questions.explanation: A value already loaded into memory may not reflect updated account data. Check framework reload behavior and use fresh data before important decisions.
questions.learningObjective: Assess caches after CPI and explain why

questions.question: Even if a bridge receiver permits only an official forwarder, it may still need to check which app on the remote chain sent the command.
questions.explanation: Not every official-bridge user has the same authority. Authenticate the delivery route, original sending app, and source domain together.
questions.learningObjective: Assess separate source authentication and explain why

questions.question: With debt unchanged, withdrawing collateral that has positive weighted value automatically increases HF even without other changes.
questions.explanation: Weighted collateral decreases while debt remains unchanged, so HF falls. Do not confuse repayment with withdrawal or total assets with recognized risk-adjusted value.
questions.learningObjective: Assess collateral withdrawals and explain why

questions.question: Repaying all principal alone always proves that debt is zero in a system with accrued interest and unpaid fees.
questions.explanation: If debt includes interest and fees, amounts beyond principal must also be settled. Check repayments against current total debt and rounding at raw-unit precision.
questions.learningObjective: Assess debt accounting and explain why

questions.question: If the face value of securities held by an issuer exceeds liabilities, market discounts and disposal costs can always be ignored when valuing reserves.
questions.explanation: Recoverable amounts can differ from face value, with discounts and costs on immediate sale. Apply valuation criteria suited to the purpose and redemption horizon.
questions.learningObjective: Assess asset valuation and explain why

questions.question: When interpreting a sender from the calldata suffix using ERC-2771, it is unnecessary to check whether the caller is a trusted forwarder.
questions.explanation: Trusting any caller's suffix permits impersonation. Verify trusted forwarders together with correct format and context handling.
questions.learningObjective: Assess meta-transactions and explain why

questions.question: In multipath Lightning payments, associating parts with the same payment and binding total amounts and settlement conditions also matters when some routes fail.
questions.explanation: Splitting uses available liquidity, but settlement of the parts must remain coordinated. Without payment identification and overall-condition checks, partial completion can be handled incorrectly.
questions.learningObjective: Assess links between partial payments and explain why

questions.question: Reusing the same idempotency key for two distinct withdrawal requests can cause a legitimate new request to be mistaken for the earlier one.
questions.explanation: Idempotency keys should remain the same for retries of one operation and differ across operations. Manage matching between keys and request content, as well as retention periods.
questions.learningObjective: Assess idempotency collisions and explain why

questions.question: If a hypothetical pool's trading fees total 60, with 10 going to the protocol and 50 to LPs, calculating LP returns using the full 60 overstates them.
questions.explanation: Return calculations must use the share LPs actually receive. Total trading fees, protocol revenue, and LP income are distinct quantities.
questions.learningObjective: Assess fee distributions and explain why

questions.question: Recording an external report's hash on-chain allows later checks for identical bytes but does not automatically verify that every statement in the report is true.
questions.explanation: Integrity commitments provide a different guarantee from content accuracy. Fact verification and trust in authors or measurement processes need separate evidence.
questions.learningObjective: Assess raw-data and factual-truth claims and explain why

questions.question: Deploying identical contract bytecode on several chains necessarily makes the whole system behave identically, even with different external-call target code, state, and administrator settings.
questions.explanation: Execution depends on stored state, environment, and external dependencies as well as local code. Distinguish matching code hashes from semantic equivalence of entire systems.
questions.learningObjective: Assess execution-environment equivalence and explain why

questions.question: A strategy whose combined spot and futures price profit and loss is zero cannot suffer liquidation from insufficient margin in its futures account.
questions.explanation: If spot gains are held elsewhere, the futures account may not obtain needed margin immediately. Overall economic hedging differs from account-level liquidity and liquidation conditions.
questions.learningObjective: Assess hedging and liquidation and explain why

questions.question: A download service checking NFT ownership can block new downloads after a sale, but automatically reclaiming local files lawfully downloaded earlier is a separate problem.
questions.explanation: On-chain eligibility checks at access time differ from control over data already provided. Distribution policies must consider copying and off-chain storage after download.
questions.learningObjective: Assess token gating and explain why

questions.question: With collateral A worth USD 600 at an 80% threshold, B worth USD 400 at a 50% threshold, and debt of USD 680, HF based on weighted collateral is 1.
questions.explanation: Weighted collateral is 600×0.8+400×0.5=680 dollars, giving 1 when divided by debt. A simple average threshold or total collateral alone produces different results.
questions.learningObjective: Assess collateral weights and explain why

questions.question: For an inverse long defined by Q×(1/Pentry−1/Pexit) BTC, a price increase makes BTC profit and loss positive with other conditions unchanged.
questions.explanation: A higher exit price has a smaller reciprocal, making the expression in parentheses positive. Calculate the absolute result and dollar conversion separately using exit price and contract quantity.
questions.learningObjective: Assess inverse-contract profit and loss and explain why

questions.question: If an interest-rate curve rises more steeply at high utilization, even a small additional loan can cause a large rate change in that region.
questions.explanation: A steep segment creates a larger rate response to utilization changes. Consider total pool size, remaining liquidity, and the relevant rate segment together.
questions.learningObjective: Assess piecewise interest rates and explain why

questions.question: A customer verifying a valid Merkle path for their own liability entry also proves that every other customer is included without omission.
questions.explanation: Inclusion of one item does not prove completeness of the whole set. Liability scope, omission prevention, and correct aggregation require separate validation.
questions.learningObjective: Assess liability-inclusion proofs and explain why

questions.question: If a source-chain deposit disappears after representation tokens are finalized on the destination chain, a bridge without a compensating mechanism can develop a collateral shortfall.
questions.explanation: Chains have different confirmation and reorganization rules. Changes on one side are not automatically reversed on the other, requiring confirmation policies and emergency responses.
questions.learningObjective: Assess finality mismatches and explain why

questions.question: Even if each source chain starts nonces at 1, using only the nonce as a destination processing-record key can never create collisions between legitimate messages from different chains.
questions.explanation: The same nonce can recur across domains. Bind a namespace matching its uniqueness scope, such as source-chain and application identifiers.
questions.learningObjective: Assess global nonce assumptions and explain why

questions.question: Even with unchanged prices, lowering collateral recognition ratios or liquidation thresholds can worsen risk for existing borrowing accounts.
questions.explanation: Lower valuation weights reduce recognized collateral. Consider the transition period and impact of governance parameter changes as well as price shocks.
questions.learningObjective: Assess collateral recognition ratios and explain why

questions.question: Whenever new borrowing is paused for risk reasons, unconditionally blocking repayment and collateral additions too minimizes user losses in every circumstance.
questions.explanation: Repayment and collateral additions can help users restore account health. Choose which functions to stop or keep available according to the attack type, asset risks, and recovery procedures.
questions.learningObjective: Assess emergency functions and explain why

questions.question: Even with a direct transfer-amount limit on a session key, unlimited approval to arbitrary spenders can create indirect movement paths that weaken the limit's purpose.
questions.explanation: Approval-based transfers such as transferFrom follow a different path from direct transfers. Check whether restrictions cover approvals and call targets too.
questions.learningObjective: Assess session-key approvals and explain why

questions.question: A block explorer's success status means the specified recipient, economic price conditions, and the merchant's business processing all completed exactly as the user intended.
questions.explanation: Execution success is a technical status related to whether execution reverted. Actual recipients, prices, assets, and off-chain business status require separate checks.
questions.learningObjective: Assess completion-status interpretations and explain why

questions.question: A correctly signed request may still be outside a gas sponsor's permitted activities, making target, function, and cumulative-cost checks meaningful.
questions.explanation: Signatures establish requester authority and consent, not the sponsor's business and budget policies. Limit costs from excessive calls or inappropriate targets.
questions.learningObjective: Assess gas sponsorship and explain why

questions.question: After checking a timeout on their own computer, a sender can refund underlying assets without duplicate-payment risk regardless of whether the destination chain received the transfer.
questions.explanation: Refunding on the source side a transfer already processed at the destination can duplicate value. Verify receipt or nonreceipt status together with timeout conditions.
questions.learningObjective: Assess IBC refunds and explain why

questions.question: Tripling the square-root price representing token1/token0 makes the price ratio nine times larger when the two tokens have equal decimals.
questions.explanation: Price is the square of the square-root value, so the multiplier is 3 squared. Raw-price scaling and token-decimal adjustments must also match.
questions.learningObjective: Assess concentrated-liquidity units and explain why

questions.question: Rounding allocations down to integers can make total user distributions smaller than the available amount, so a remainder policy is needed.
questions.explanation: Truncation from small allocations can accumulate across many entries. Design accounting and carry-forward rules so payouts plus the remainder equal the total.
questions.learningObjective: Assess integer truncation and explain why

questions.question: A contract can convert a 6-decimal token's raw amount to an 18-decimal raw scale by multiplying by 10^12 while preserving the displayed quantity.
questions.explanation: The difference between 6 and 18 decimal places is 12, giving a multiplier of 10^12. Actual calculations must also check range, overflow, and return units.
questions.learningObjective: Assess precision preservation and explain why

questions.question: If spending a 900 sat UTXO adds a 70 vB input at 15 sat/vB, the input alone costs 1,050 sat and its net contribution is negative.
questions.explanation: The added fee is 70×15=1,050 sat, exceeding the UTXO by 150 sat. Selecting it may be uneconomic even before other transaction costs.
questions.learningObjective: Assess input economics and explain why

questions.question: A past successful eth_call with identical function arguments guarantees the actual transaction will succeed even if permissions or balances change afterward.
questions.explanation: A past call reflects state at that moment. Nonces, balances, approvals, prices, and code can change before actual execution, so it is not a guarantee of success.
questions.learningObjective: Assess simulation guarantees and explain why
